Article Title: Ex-Air chief AP Singh wrote to Rajnath, urged him to keep Race Course land under IAF control
Article Text:
The sealing of the facility, which includes a golf course, swimming pool and other amenities, also led to the cancellation of a planned farewell for the outgoing Air Chief Marshal.

IAF flags operational concerns

'Absolute disgrace': Congress slams Centre over reclaiming IAF complex

Centre's drive to reclaim prime land

NEW DELHI: Days before retiring as chief of air staff, Air Chief Marshal AP Singh wrote to defence minister Rajnath Singh , raising concerns over the sealing of the Indian Air Force's (IAF) sports complex at the Race Course Air Force Station in New Delhi.In a letter dated October 26, Air Chief Marshal AP Singh urged the defence minister to ensure that the over 40-acre land parcel remained under the Air Force's control, news agency PTI reported, citing people familiar with the matter.AP Singh also raised the issue during an in-person meeting with Rajnath Singh on October 29, three days before his retirement on October 31. He sought the minister's intervention after authorities under the ministry of housing and urban affairs (MoHUA) sealed the sports complex, triggering concern within defence circles, as reported by PTI.The sealing of the facility, which includes a golf course, swimming pool and other amenities, also led to the cancellation of a planned farewell for the outgoing Air Chief Marshal.There has been no official statement from either the IAF or the defence ministry on the matter.In his letter, AP Singh referred to a joint survey of the land parcel conducted in 2014 by the then ministry of urban development, the Defence Estate Department and the Air Force.He argued that the land should remain with the IAF, citing the sports complex's important role in the overall functioning of the air station.The Air Force has also conveyed its objections to the defence ministry and sought the cancellation of the sealing process, the people said.It has highlighted the operational importance of the Race Course Air Force Station, particularly its role in addressing potential aerial security threats in the high-security zone around the Prime Minister's residence.AP Singh also referred to the station's history and its existing land arrangement in his communication. The complex comprises three distinct segments of land, and he stressed that all its facilities should continue to function as usual.The Congress on Tuesday criticised the Centre's move to reclaim the land housing the Indian Air Force Sports Complex, accusing the Modi government of showing "utter disrespect" to the IAF community.Congress general secretary in-charge of communications Jairam Ramesh shared a media report on X which said that Air Chief Marshal AP Singh had written to defence minister Rajnath Singh.In his post, Ramesh said, "The IAF Sports Complex has a long history and has, over the decades, served many public purposes, as well as being an integral part of the Indian Air Force social infrastructure.""The Modi government's actions are an absolute disgrace and show utter disrespect to the entire IAF family," Ramesh added.The sealing is part of a wider government exercise to reclaim high-value land parcels in the vicinity of Lok Kalyan Marg.Over the past several weeks, the land and development Office (L&DO), under the Union housing and urban affairs ministry, has reviewed plots being used for defence golf courses and sports facilities.The ministry had earlier asked the concerned authorities to hand over the land housing the Air Force Golf Course. The L&DO subsequently issued eviction notices to the sports complex's management, seeking the return of the land.The government has also taken action against other establishments occupying prime land in the area.In August, the department evicted the Delhi Race Club from its 53-acre premises on Lok Kalyan Marg, citing the requirement of the land for an unspecified public purpose.It also reclaimed the Jaipur Polo Ground from the India Polo Association, citing broader public purposes, governance and defence infrastructure projects.
Article Summary: Air Chief Marshal AP Singh wrote to defence minister Rajnath Singh. He raised concerns over the sealing of the Indian Air Force's sports complex. The complex includes a golf course, swimming pool and other amenities. sealing is part of a wider government exercise to reclaim high-value land parcels.

Article Title: 'Huge impact on polls': IB opposes shifting convict in ex-Punjab CM Beant Singh's assassination to state jail
Article Text:
Ex-Punjab CM murdered on August 31, 1995

Why is Hawara seeking a transfer?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Intelligence Bureau (IB) on Tuesday opposed the transfer of Jagtar Singh Hawara, convicted in the 1995 assassination of then-Punjab chief minister Beant Singh, from Delhi's Tihar Jail to a prison in Punjab, telling the Supreme Court that the move could have a “huge impact” on the upcoming assembly elections in the state.The agency also classified Hawara as a high-risk prisoner and said he should not be shifted to Punjab. A bench of Justices M M Sundresh and P B Varale described the IB report as “very damning” while hearing Hawara's plea seeking a transfer to a prison in his home state.Senior advocate S Muralidhar, appearing for Hawara, told the court, “If elections are a concern, this may be taken up after three months.” The Supreme Court posted the matter for hearing in February next year. Elections to the 117-member Punjab Assembly are due early next year.Beant Singh, who served as Punjab chief minister from 1992 to 1995, was killed in a suicide bombing outside the state civil secretariat in Chandigarh on August 31, 1995. The blast also killed 16 others. Hawara, a member of the banned Babbar Khalsa International, was convicted in the assassination case and is serving a life sentence for the remainder of his natural life.Hawara's plea argues that he is a native of Punjab's Fatehgarh Sahib district and should be allowed to serve his sentence in a prison in the state. It also says there are no cases pending against him in Delhi and that his conduct in prison has been without blemish, apart from a jailbreak in January 2004.Hawara was among four inmates who escaped from Chandigarh's high-security Burail Jail on January 22, 2004, by digging a nearly 100-foot-long tunnel. The other escapees were Paramjit Singh Bheora, Jagtar Singh Tara and Devi Singh. Hawara and Bheora were subsequently arrested, while Tara was caught in Thailand. Devi Singh remains absconding.Opposing the transfer, Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati, appearing for the Delhi government, had earlier told the Supreme Court that Hawara's jailbreak history raised the risk of another escape. She also cited a Union home ministry advisory on the transfer of high-risk prisoners and the Punjab government's concerns over the possible impact on law and order.Hawara was sentenced to death by a trial court in March 2007. The Punjab and Haryana High Court commuted the sentence to life imprisonment in October 2010, directing that he should not be released for the rest of his life. Appeals against the high court verdict are pending before the Supreme Court.
Article Summary: Jagtar Singh Hawara was convicted in the 1995 assassination of then-Punjab chief minister Beant Singh. Hawara is serving a life sentence for the remainder of his natural life. He is seeking a transfer to a prison in his home state of Punjab. Elections to the 117-member Punjab Assembly are due early next year.

Article Title: J&K: Omar Abdullah faces setback as Srinagar MP Aga Ruhullah quits NC, resigns from Parliament
Article Text:
Aga Ruhullah announces resignation as Srinagar MP

NEW DELHI: In a major setback to the ruling National Conference in Jammu and Kashmir , Srinagar Lok Sabha member Aga Syed Ruhullah Mehdi on Tuesday formally announced his resignation from the parliamentary seat and party on the 26th death anniversary of his father.Mehdi hinted at forming a new political party led by "honest and compassionate people," as news agency PTI reported.A day earlier, banners at the entrance of Mehdi's residence in Srinagar had offered a glimpse of the message he wanted to convey. One read, “Wada kursi se bada hai” (a promise is bigger than a chair), while the other said, “Kirdar ki siyasat, usoolon ki siyasat” (politics of character, politics of principles).One party worker said, “even at a barber's shop, people do not give up their chairs for someone else even if that person is older. Here is a man willing to leave his chair for the sake of principles. Who gives up a chair like that.”Mehdi's resignation comes amid growing discontent within the ruling party, with Jammu and Kashmir chief minister Omar Abdullah facing a revolt by a section of NC legislators.Around 25 legislators have reportedly demanded the replacement of all eight cabinet ministers, including the deputy chief minister, within 15 days.They have also sought the removal of Nasir Aslam Wani, Omar Abdullah's close aide and political adviser.At a meeting held at the residence of NC MLA Qaiser Jamshaid Lone on Friday evening, the legislators passed a resolution seeking a cabinet overhaul and wider consultations within the party before portfolios are allocated.Around 18 MLAs attended the meeting in person, while seven joined online, according to a legislator who was present.The NC has 41 MLAs in the 90-member Jammu and Kashmir assembly. It runs a coalition government with the support of six Congress MLAs, six independent legislators and one CPM member.
Article Summary: Aga Syed Ruhullah Mehdi formally announced his resignation from the parliamentary seat and party on the 26th death anniversary of his father. Mehdi hinted at forming a new political party led by "honest and compassionate people" Mehdi's resignation comes amid growing discontent within the ruling party.

Article Title: 'Gaddar': BJP accuses Rahul Gandhi of treason, calls him 'Bhasmasur'
Article Text:
Bhatia described Rahul Gandhi as a destructive force and accused him of promoting anarchy instead of respecting India's democratic framework.

'Bhasmasur': BJP accuses Rahul of seeking to strangle democracy

'People will end your political careers': BJP warns Rahul, Mamata and Tejashwi

BJP questions Rahul's foreign meetings, demands answers on China MoU

BJP accuses Rahul of inappropriate conduct with woman police officer

'They want to overthrow elected governments': BJP targets opposition

NEW DELHI: Bharatiya Janata Party ( BJP ) on Tuesday launched a scathing attack on Congress leader and leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi , accusing him of treason, promoting anarchy and attempting to undermine India's democratic institutions.BJP national spokesperson Gaurav Bhatia labelled Rahul Gandhi 'gaddar' (traitor) and 'Bhasmasur', alleging that his political approach was aimed at destabilising the country and weakening its constitutional framework.Addressing a press conference in New Delhi, Bhatia questioned Rahul Gandhi's foreign engagements, raised allegations over the Congress's memorandum of understanding (MoU) with the Communist Party of China (CCP) and demanded answers about the alleged funding of protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar."This issue is about the model of anarchy, disorder, and treason that the Leader of the Opposition is presenting to the country... That is why he is being referred to as 'Rahul Gaddar'," Bhatia said.He also accused Rahul of advocating unconstitutional regime change and attempting to weaken democratic institutions.Bhatia described Rahul Gandhi as a destructive force and accused him of promoting anarchy instead of respecting India's democratic framework."If India has one greatest strength, it lies in its democratic government, its reverence for the Constitution, and the stability it has maintained for 12 years. On the other hand, there is an opposition that is anarchic in its thinking, anti-Constitution, and openly speaks of overthrowing the government. Rahul Gandhi believes in anarchy and destruction; it is not for nothing that he is called a 'Bhasmasura' (a destructive force). He has become the kind of leader who seeks to usher in anarchy by killing democracy, strangling it to death," he said.The BJP spokesperson alleged that the opposition was seeking to overthrow elected governments and undermine constitutional institutions, including Parliament and the Supreme Court."The other ideology says that whatever you build, our only task is to destroy it. That is why Rahul Gandhi is not called Bhasmasur without reason. If anyone is attempting to destroy these institutions, it is Rahul Gandhi," he said.Bhatia also targeted Gandhi, former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee and former Bihar deputy chief minister Tejashwi Yadav over their alleged support for regime change.He warned that repeated calls for regime change could instead turn public opinion against the opposition and threaten the political future of its leaders."I say this with a lot of responsibility: people wanting a regime change might witness a situation where the people of the country feel that the Opposition is irresponsible and should be changed. The public will find an alternative to the opposition; do not imagine, Rahul Gandhi, Mamata Banerjee, or Tejashwi Yadav, that you will gain anything through anarchy. This public will put an end to your political careers. India’s democracy will remain unscathed," he said.The remarks came amid a controversy over the use of the phrase 'regime change' by senior advocate Prashant Bhushan, All India Students Association (AISA) president Neha Bora and Congress spokesperson Pawan Khera during public statements and press conferences in Delhi.The comments were made in the context of protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Bhatia also questioned Rahul Gandhi's meetings with foreign figures, including US Congresswoman Ilhan Omar and Mushfiqul Fazal, whom he accused of adopting anti-India positions."How can the leader of opposition in India be anti-India? How can he betray the nation?... The central question is why Rahul Gandhi is meeting individuals like Ilhan Omar or Mushfiqul Fazal who adopt anti-India stances. Is there any discussion about weakening India and bringing about regime change?" he asked.He further demanded that Gandhi disclose the contents of the Congress's MoU with the Communist Party of China and explain the alleged funding behind protests."Rahul Gandhi signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Communist Party of China (CCP) but has not disclosed what it contains to this day... He must also clarify where the funding for these protests, which are being organized with the aim of creating anarchy, is coming from."The BJP spokesperson also accused Gandhi of inappropriate physical conduct with a woman police officer during an anti-CEC protest on Ashoka Road near Jantar Mantar."Rahul Gandhi's inappropriate touching of a woman police officer is disgraceful. No political position gives anyone the right to touch a woman inappropriately. He must answer for his shameful behaviour," Bhatia said.He argued that Gandhi's position as Leader of the Opposition did not give him the right to behave inappropriately with security personnel.In his concluding remarks, Bhatia accused Rahul Gandhi and other opposition leaders of attempting to weaken India's democratic institutions and destabilise elected governments."Wherever there is an elected government, they want to overthrow it. They want to destroy constitutional institutions such as the Supreme Court and Parliament, as well as historical monuments," he said.The BJP leader maintained that India's democratic framework and constitutional institutions would remain strong despite what he described as the opposition's attempts to create disorder.
Article Summary: BJP national spokesperson Gaurav Bhatia labelled Rahul Gandhi 'gaddar' (traitor) and 'Bhasmasur' Alleges that his political approach was aimed at destabilising the country and weakening its constitutional framework. Accuses Rahul of advocating unconstitutional regime change and attempting to weaken democracy.

Article Title: Indian national killed as helicopters collide near Mount Everest in Nepal
Article Text:
An official said that one helicopter was travelling from Lukla, while the other was returning from Gorakhpur, near the Everest base camp. Both reportedly attempted to land at the same spot.

Who were injured in the collision?

Who were inside the helicopters

Where did the accident take place?

An Indian national was killed and three others, including a New Zealand resident of Indian origin, were injured in a helicopter crash in Nepal. The two helicopters collided while attempting to land near Mount Everest in Nepal on Tuesday morning.The accident took place at around 8.11am (local time) at Pheriche in Ward 4 of Khumbu Pasang Lhamu Rural Municipality in Solukhumbu district.A video of the incident has captured the moment the two aircraft collided, highlighting the dangers of helicopter operations in the busy Everest region.Nepal Police confirmed the casualties from the accident in a statement. They said, "Solukhumbu accident further update: One person dead, three injured"Police identified the deceased as 47-year-old Vasanth Kumar Balaramaramadu, an Indian national travelling aboard the Fishtail Air helicopter. His body was taken to a hospital in Lukla.49-year-old Shailesh Krishna Patel, an Indian-origin resident of New Zealand, was also injured who was travelling aboard the Fishtail Air helicopter. He was airlifted to Mediciti Hospital in Kathmandu by a Prabhu helicopter, police inspector Mausam Tamang said.The other two injured pilots were identified as Rabindra Prajapati of Fishtail Air and Prajwal KC of Air Dynasty.Both were taken to Kathmandu for further treatment.Three people were injured in the accident, including two pilots and a passenger.Police inspector Mausam Tamang identified the injured passenger as Shailesh Krishna Patel, a 49-year-old Indian-origin resident of New Zealand. He was travelling aboard the Fishtail Air helicopter along with Balaramaramadu.Patel was airlifted to Mediciti Hospital in Kathmandu for treatment in a Prabhu helicopter, Tamang said.The two injured Nepali pilots were identified as Rabindra Prajapati of Fishtail Air and Prajwal KC of Air Dynasty. Both were taken to Kathmandu for further medical treatment.Fishtail Air said its helicopter was carrying tourists who had been rescued from the Everest region when it crashed while attempting to land. A company official confirmed that Balaramaramadu and Patel were among the passengers.The Air Dynasty helicopter, meanwhile, was carrying cargo, according to an official from the company.Solukhumbu chief district officer Kaman Singh Thapa Magar confirmed the collision to Reuters and said the injured New Zealand passenger had been rescued.Police have yet to confirm the total number of people aboard the two helicopters at the time of the accident.Pheriche is a settlement along the route to the Mount Everest base camp, around 150 km north-east of Kathmandu. It is an important stop for trekkers and climbers heading towards the world's highest mountain.The collision occurred during Nepal's peak trekking season, when helicopter services are widely used to ferry tourists, mountaineers and rescued trekkers across the Everest region.The exact cause of the collision remains unclear. Police said they were collecting further details about the incident.Civil Aviation Authority of Nepal (CAAN) deputy spokesperson Gyanendra Bhul said that the helicopters were approaching the landing area from different directions when the accident occurred, BBC Nepali reported.According to Bhul, one helicopter was travelling from Lukla, while the other was returning from Gorakhpur, near the Everest base camp. Both reportedly attempted to land at the same spot."It appears that the accident occurred when helicopters travelling from Lukla and returning from Gorakhpur, near the base camp, tried to land at the same place," Bhul said.The exact cause of the collision remains unclear. However, preliminary information suggests that snow-covered helipads may have played a role in the accident."It looks like they tried to land on one of the other helipads, perhaps because it was covered in snow, even though there were other helipads," he said.The authorities have not yet released further details about the identities of those involved or the circumstances leading to the collision.
Article Summary: The two helicopters collided while attempting to land near Mount Everest in Nepal on Tuesday morning. One helicopter was travelling from Lukla, while the other was returning from Gorakhpur, near the Everest base camp. Both reportedly attempted to land at the same spot. An Indian national was killed and three others, including a New Zealand resident of Indian origin, were injured.

Article Title: Bengaluru man holds woman at knifepoint, threatens to kill her in full public view during gold chain snatching bid
Article Text:
In Bengaluru's Indiranagar, a woman named Jayashree was attacked while working at a shop

Locals overpower accused, rescue woman

Accused arrested, remanded to judicial custody





BENGALURU: A woman working at a shop in Bengaluru's Indiranagar was held at knifepoint, threatened with murder and had her hands stuck to a table with Fevikwik after a man barged into the shop and attempted to snatch her gold chain on October 31.Alert locals rushed to her rescue, overpowered the accused and handed him over to the police.The incident occurred around 11.45am in the Indiranagar police station limits. The accused, identified as Prabhuraj alias Raj, allegedly walked into the shop and initially pretended that someone was chasing him and trying to kill him, asking the woman to shelter him.However, he soon turned on her, allegedly pulling out a knife and holding it against her neck. He threatened her and demanded her gold chain, reportedly weighing 35 grams and valued at around Rs 4.5 lakh.In an attempt to prevent her from resisting or escaping, the accused allegedly poured Fevikwik on both her hands and stuck them to the shop table. He then attempted to take the chain from her neck.The woman screamed for help as the accused tried to snatch her chain. Hearing her cries, neighbouring shopkeepers and passersby rushed into the shop.Realising that he was surrounded, Prabhuraj held the knife against her neck and threatened to kill her if anyone came closer. He allegedly tried to use the woman as a shield to escape from the crowd.However, locals managed to divert his attention, overpower him and rescue the woman before handing him over to Indiranagar police.The woman was subsequently rescued and taken to hospital. She was reported to have escaped without serious injuries.Police registered a case at Indiranagar police station and arrested Prabhuraj. He was subsequently remanded to judicial custody.The accused reportedly worked as a delivery agent. Police are verifying his background and investigating the circumstances surrounding the attempted chain snatching.A video showing the accused threatening the woman and dragging her during the incident has since surfaced on social media, triggering concern over the safety of people working in shops.
Article Summary: A woman working at a shop in Bengaluru's Indiranagar was held at knifepoint, threatened with murder and had her hands stuck to a table with Fevikwik.Alert locals rushed to her rescue, overpowered the accused and handed him over to the police. He was subsequently remanded to judicial custody.

Article Title: ‘Mother-in-law responsible if anything happens to me’: Pune techie's last message before she was found hanging in flat; husband held
Article Text:
Payal Zambre Patil was found hanging in a flat in Mukund Nagar following conflicts with her mother-in-law.

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you believe that family disputes can lead to tragic outcomes? Yes, very much No, not usually 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





PUNE: A 29-year-old woman, daughter-in-law of a prominent businessman in Pune, was found hanging from a ceiling fan in a flat in Mukund Nagar on Monday morning, following an alleged dispute with her mother-in-law.Police arrested her husband and registered a case of harassment and abetment of suicide against four members of her in-laws' family after her relatives accused them of subjecting her to harassment over repeated demands for gold.According to news agency PTI, the deceased, Payal Zambre Patil, was an IT professional before she quit her job.She was married to Akshay Zambre Patil, and the couple has a three-year-old daughter.Senior inspector Yashwant Nikam of Swargate police station said Payal lived with her in-laws in Mukund Nagar, off Pune-Satara Road. On Monday morning, she allegedly sent messages to some people stating that her mother-in-law would be responsible if anything happened to her.Police said Payal had an argument with her mother-in-law on Sunday and left her matrimonial home. Her family and in-laws began searching for her on Monday morning.She was eventually found hanging from a ceiling fan in another flat in an apartment complex near their residence. The incident came to light around 11.30am."When police reached the apartment, she was found hanging from the ceiling. No suicide note was found," a Swargate police station official said, adding that statements of her maternal relatives were being recorded.Payal's brother, Rishikesh Pawar, alleged that her husband and in-laws appeared unconcerned when he reached their home on Monday morning. He claimed they began searching for her only after the family questioned them.According to Pawar, the in-laws returned within five minutes and informed them that Payal was in a nearby apartment. He alleged that the flat's door was locked from inside and he managed to enter through the rear balcony, where he found his sister hanging.He further claimed that Payal had repeatedly complained about harassment by her mother-in-law. Recalling Sunday's argument, Pawar said he had called Akshay and told him that the dispute was temporary and could be resolved.Payal's uncle alleged that she had been harassed over demands for gold since her marriage. He claimed her in-laws demanded 10 tolas of gold every Diwali."This year too, they demanded gold, but we told them that we were farmers and, given the drought-like situation, it was not possible for us to meet the demand. We had even promised to give the gold next year," he alleged.The complaint filed by Payal's family also accused her husband and in-laws of mentally harassing her during her pregnancy in 2022 by pressuring her to give birth to a boy. After she delivered a girl on March 30, 2023, her in-laws allegedly argued with her at the hospital and said they would not take responsibility for either her or the child, the complaint stated.Following her death, relatives from Payal's parental family allegedly vandalised her in-laws' residence, office and marriage hall, triggering tension in the area. Her father-in-law owns a marriage hall and an eatery on Pune-Satara Road, police said. Her parental family runs a business in the Khed-Shivapur area.Swargate police registered a case of harassment and abetment of suicide against four people, including Payal's husband and mother-in-law. Senior inspector Nikam said Akshay had been arrested and two police teams were formed to trace the remaining accused.While Payal's family has alleged that she was murdered and her death staged as suicide, police have registered a case of abetment of suicide. The circumstances surrounding her death are being investigated.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: Payal Zambre Patil, 29, was found hanging from a ceiling fan in a flat in Mukund Nagar on Monday morning. Police arrested her husband and registered a case of harassment and abetment of suicide against four members of her in-laws' family. Her relatives accused them of subjecting her to harassment over demands for gold.

Article Title: Major fire breaks out at HPCL Visakhapatnam refinery, no casualties
Article Text:
A fire occurred at Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited Visakh Refinery during the night, alarming nearby residents.





VISAKHAPATNAM: A fire that broke out at Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited's (HPCL) Visakhapatnam refinery in Malkapuram on Monday night was brought under control, with no casualties or injuries reported.The fire was confined to a pitch intermediate storage tank in the refinery's sulfur unit, and all units at the facility are operating safely, HPCL said.In a post on X, the company said the fire was reported around 10pm on November 2, following which its Fire and Safety Team immediately activated firefighting and emergency response measures."The fire was localised to the pitch tank area and was brought under control within a short time. There have been no casualties," HPCL said, adding that all refinery units were functioning safely.Malkapuram Circle Inspector E Narasimha Rao said the fire involved sulfur pitch, a waste or bottom product generated in the refinery's sulfur unit. He said HPCL's own fire tenders were deployed to tackle the blaze and no external assistance was required."There are no casualties, no injuries and no major issues. Everyone is safe, and there is no need for panic," he said.Revenue Divisional Officer (RDO) Dileep Chakravarthy, who visited the site, said the fire had been completely extinguished using the firefighting equipment installed at the refinery and resources deployed by the Andhra Pradesh Fire Department.He said a small blast was reported at the facility before the fire broke out. Chakravarthy added that an enquiry would be initiated to examine industrial safety at the facility in accordance with applicable norms."There is no cause for worry, and no injuries or casualties have been reported. People are requested not to panic about the incident," he said.Meanwhile, eyewitnesses said the flames rising from the refinery were large enough to frighten people in the vicinity. One eyewitness said people moved away from the area after seeing the blaze.
Article Summary: A fire broke out at Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited's (HPCL) Visakhapatnam refinery on Monday night. No casualties or injuries were reported. The fire was confined to a pitch intermediate storage tank in the refinery's sulfur unit.

Article Title: Days after Farooq’s Pak praise, Mehbooba says Abdullahs created distrust between Kashmir & rest of India
Article Text:
Mehbooba Mufti accuses NC of widening Kashmir’s divide with rest of India, urges Centre to hold talks.

SRINAGAR: Days after National Conference president Farooq Abdullah made a controversial statement hailing Pakistan’s diplomatic efforts on Kashmir , PDP president Mehbooba Mufti Monday launched an attack on the NC leadership across generations, accusing it of creating distrust between Kashmir and the rest of the country.Addressing party workers in Srinagar on PDP’s foundation day, she said: “NC’s policies, dating back to the days of Sheikh Mohammad Abdullah, have created a wedge between Kashmir and the rest of the country. Unlike them, my father, Mufti Mohammad Sayeed, tried everything to bridge this gap.”“If there is any party that has betrayed Kashmiris, it is NC. As long as it remains in power, there will be no peace in Jammu & Kashmir,” Mehbooba said, urging party members to make efforts to regain power.She said if Kashmiris have suffered over the years, it was because of Sheikh Abdullah, who repeatedly changed his political positions, from supporting Kashmir’s accession to India to raising slogans for a plebiscite and Pakistan.Farooq was following in his father’s footsteps by recently stating that Pakistan’s diplomatic efforts were saving Kashmiris, portraying the neighbouring country as the “saviour” of Kashmiris.“This conveys a message to New Delhi that Kashmiris are with Pakistan and they should be oppressed, arrested and have their passports seized,” she said.“NC’s forte has been to defame Kashmiris since 1947,” she added.Targeting chief minister Omar Abdullah, she said he keeps blaming PDP for his failures, while he has failed to provide jobs to the people.The PDP chief also trained guns on the Union govt, accusing it of suppressing the voice of Kashmiris. She alleged that the Centre splintered her party after the abrogation of Article 370 , “but we are not among those who change political positions”.“The Govt of India must understand that the people of J&Kare the crown of India. If you trample upon this crown, you too will also suffer,” she said.“This is the land of rishis and peers (Sufi saints). If you do wrong to this land, you will not remain safe,” Mehbooba further said, adding: “How long will you govern us through suspicion? You must trust us the way (former prime minister) Atal Bihari Vajpayee trusted us.”She emphasised initiating talks, stating that Kashmiris will not be governed by force indefinitely.
Article Summary: Mehbooba Mufti accuses NC of widening Kashmir’s divide with rest of India, urges Centre to hold talks. “If there is any party that has betrayed Kashmiris, it is NC. As long as it remains in power, there will be no peace in Jammu & Kashmir,” she said.

Article Title: 'You became PM because of foreign help': Rahul Gandhi challenges PM Modi for debate
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi on Monday launched a scathing attack on Prime Minister Narendra Modi , accusing him of becoming PM because of "foreign help".In a social media post on X, Rahul alleged that PM Modi's financial system was fully controlled and supported by foreigners, while foreign social media platforms fully backed him."Mr Modi, stop lying to this nation," the Congress leader said."You became PM because of foreign help. You remain PM because of foreign help. Your financial system is fully controlled and supported by foreigners. Foreign social media fully backs you," he added.Rahul also challenged PM Modi to an open debate on the issue, but said the latter would not dare to accept it."I challenge you to an open debate about this. Any stage, any time. Come if you have the guts. Article Text:

India and Israel have voted against a Pakistan- and Belarus-sponsored draft resolution at the united nations seeking conventional arms control at regional and subregional levels, with New Delhi arguing that national security concerns cannot be restricted by geographical boundaries.The draft resolution, titled ‘General and complete disarmament: Conventional arms control at the regional and subregional levels’, was adopted by the UN general assembly’s First Committee on Monday, receiving 180 votes in favour, two against and no abstentions.According to the news agency PTI, India and Israel were the only two countries among the 193 UN member states to oppose the resolution.Explaining India's position, Anmol Sher Bedi, first secretary at India's permanent mission to the UN, maintained that conventional arms control was a global issue and should not be addressed primarily through regional and subregional frameworks.“We are not fully convinced that it should be pursued primarily in regional and sub-regional contexts,” Bedi said while presenting India's explanation of vote before the UNGA first committee.He added that New Delhi's opposition was in line with its consistent position on the matter.India also raised questions over the resolution's call for the UN disarmament commission to develop principles that could provide a framework for regional agreements on conventional arms control.“We read this request with a certain degree of curiosity,” Bedi said, pointing out that the commission had already reached three consensus-based outcomes on related issues.These included guidelines and recommendations on regional disarmament adopted in 1993, guidelines on conventional arms control and disarmament finalised in 1999, and recommendations on practical confidence-building measures concerning conventional weapons agreed upon in 2017.“That makes three consensus outcomes on this very subject in the very body now being asked to start from scratch,” he said.Questioning the need for further discussions, Bedi said it was difficult to understand why an issue that had already undergone extensive deliberations needed to be taken up again, unless the intention was to keep the UN's disarmament machinery occupied.India also criticised the resolution's emphasis on maintaining a balance in defence capabilities within regional and subregional settings.Bedi argued that the approach wrongly presumed that countries' security interests were confined to their immediate geographical neighbourhoods.“This assumes that the security concerns of States politely stop at their regional borders. They do not,” he said.He further stressed that national security considerations often extend beyond narrowly defined regional boundaries, adding that the idea of maintaining a military balance within a particular region or subregion was unrealistic.The resolution argues that conventional arms control should primarily be pursued at regional and subregional levels, as most threats to international peace and security in the post-Cold War period have emerged among countries within the same geographical regions.It also calls for promoting agreements that strengthen regional peace and security while maintaining armaments and military forces at the lowest possible levels.Separately, India voted against a paragraph referring to conventional arms control proposals concerning South Asia.The paragraph took note of initiatives undertaken in various regions, including consultations among certain latin American countries and proposals for conventional arms control in South Asia, while acknowledging the importance of such measures for regional security.The resolution further states that militarily significant countries and nations possessing greater military capabilities have a special responsibility to advance agreements aimed at strengthening regional peace and security.
Article Summary: India and Israel voted against a Pakistan- and Belarus-sponsored draft resolution at the united nations seeking conventional arms control at regional and subregional levels. New Delhi argued that national security concerns cannot be restricted by geographical boundaries. The draft resolution was adopted by the UN general assembly’s First Committee on Monday.

NEW DELHI: The political row over an alleged sting operation in Karnataka intensified on Monday, with Union minister HD Kumaraswamy questioning the delay in constituting a Special Investigation Team (SIT) and challenging state minister Priyank Kharge to allow the probe to proceed. Kharge, meanwhile, alleged that a Union minister was pressuring the Modi government to use central agencies against him and his Cabinet colleagues.The exchange comes amid a police investigation into case number 56/26, registered at the Central Crime Branch (CCB) police station in connection with the alleged sting operation targeting former Karnataka chief minister Siddaramaiah.Addressing reporters in Bengaluru, Kumaraswamy questioned why the state government had not constituted the SIT, claiming that the High Court had already issued directions for such an investigation. The High Court already gave directions for the SIT, and police officers were also named. But these people went to the Supreme Court, and they have taken shelter of the Supreme Court not to actually constitute this SIT.Why have they not constituted the SIT up till now?” Kumaraswamy said.The Union minister also disputed the police account regarding the arrest of an accused in the case. Bengaluru police commissioner Seemant Kumar Singh had said on Sunday that Ritesh Pandey was arrested in New Delhi, while two other accused, Vinod Sharma and Prajwal Revanna, were absconding.Questioning the circumstances of the arrest, Kumaraswamy referred to the accused as Nitesh Kumar and claimed that he had been arrested in Ghaziabad.“Did the police officers arrest the man named Nitesh Kumar from Kumaraswamy's residence? Now you have brought that man to court. He gave his address in Ghaziabad. On 23rd October, he was arrested from Indirapuram in Ghaziabad,” he said while addressing PC.Kumaraswamy also denied Kharge's allegation that he was seeking action through central agencies or intervention from leaders in Delhi.“What is necessary for me in my life, or even for my family? Even when my brother's family was facing difficulties, we never begged anyone in Delhi,” he said.“I never asked anyone to do anything of that sort. He himself alleged that this incident was carried out by members of a Congress leader's family,” Kumaraswamy added.Accusing Congress leaders of trying to divert attention from the controversy, he called for an investigation into events dating back to 2011.“Today, they will say one thing; tomorrow, they will say something else. They want to divert attention from this issue. If we properly investigate everything dating back to 2011, ultimately...” he said.He also questioned the timing of the Bengaluru police commissioner's press release on the investigation, which was issued on Kannada Rajyotsava.“Yesterday, despite it being a public holiday and everyone celebrating Kannada Rajyotsava, what was the urgency in calling the media and publishing the press release? Why was it done in such a hurry? I know what the present Chief Minister, the DGP and other officers discussed at the stadium after the Kannada Rajyotsava celebrations. I know what they decided before going public,” he said.Kumaraswamy accused sections of the media of portraying the police statement as a setback for him.“The Bengaluru City Police Commissioner's statement has been interpreted in many different ways in the media. You have started news as if it is a boomerang for Kumaraswamy,” he said.In a post on X on Monday, Kharge alleged that a Union minister was pressuring the central government to initiate Income Tax and Enforcement Directorate action against him and other Karnataka ministers. Without naming Kumaraswamy, he claimed that the ongoing investigation into alleged irregularities in Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC) recruitment was being used as a political cover."Whispers in Delhi's corridors of power are that a union minister is desperately pressuring Modi Sarkar to weaponise the IT and ED against my Cabinet colleagues and me, using the KPSC investigation as political cover," Kharge said.He further alleged that the minister was attempting to use the ED to pressure accused persons into implicating Congress leaders in the recruitment case."The RSS's newest Group D recruit is also reportedly attempting to use the ED to pressure all accused to falsely implicate Congress leaders and me in the KPSC recruitment case," he said."It appears the extremely hard-working hon'ble minister is not prepared to go down alone. In his desperation, he seems determined to drag his own coalition partners down with him," Kharge added.Although Kharge did not name the Union minister, his remarks appeared to be directed at Kumaraswamy, who is a senior JD(S) leader and a partner of the BJP in the ruling coalition at the Centre, according to party sources cited by PTI.Police say phone was delivered to Kumaraswamy's residenceOn Sunday, Bengaluru police commissioner Seemant Kumar Singh said Ritesh Pandey had been arrested in New Delhi in connection with the alleged sting operation. Police said their investigation indicated that Pandey, accompanied by Vinod Sharma, had purchased a mobile phone from a market in Karol Bagh and subsequently delivered it to Prajwal Revanna at the official residence of Union minister HD Kumaraswamy."Ritesh Pandey has disclosed that he purchased and delivered the mobile phone at the behest of Prajwal Revanna; we are currently verifying these facts," Singh said.The commissioner said technical evidence had confirmed that the phone was purchased from the shop identified by investigators and delivered to a location within the building. He also said police had found evidence of financial dealings between Pandey and Revanna."We have uncovered evidence of financial dealings between Prajwal Revanna and Ritesh Pandey. Based on this evidence, we issued notices to both Vinod Sharma and Prajwal Revanna; however, they failed to respond and are currently absconding. We are actively searching for them," Singh said.Singh said the accused had applied for anticipatory bail, which police intended to oppose. He added that the alleged role of the individuals involved and the circumstances surrounding the delivery of the phone were still being verified."While these statements are yet to be corroborated, the technical evidence gathered thus far confirms that the three individuals were in contact with one another. Preliminary information suggests that these actions were carried out under the instructions of Prajwal Revanna, a claim that is currently being verified," he said.

This year's elections will take place on Wednesday (early Thursday, as per Indian time) with voters choosing members of Congress as well as several state and local officials.Unlike presidential elections, midterms do not decide who occupies the White House. Instead, they determine which party controls Congress for the next two years, making them a crucial test of President Donald Trump's political standing and his ability to push through his agenda.The US Congress has two chambers, the House of Representatives and the Senate, and midterm elections determine the composition of both. All 435 seats in the House are contested every two years, as members serve two-year terms.In the Senate, where members serve six-year terms, roughly one-third of the 100 seats come up for election every two years. This time, 35 Senate seats, including two special-election contests, are at stake. Alongside congressional races, voters in several states will also elect governors and other state and local officials.Republicans currently hold narrow majorities in both chambers of Congress.The 435-member House has 218 Republicans, 214 Democrats, one independent who caucuses with Republicans and two vacant seats. A party needs 218 seats for a majority.Meanwhile, the Senate has 53 Republicans and 47 Democrats and allied independents, with 51 seats required for a majority. Democrats need a net gain of four seats in each chamber to take control of both.The outcome could therefore hinge on a small number of closely contested races.The party controlling Congress has considerable influence over the president's ability to govern.Congress passes legislation, approves government spending and oversees the executive branch. The Senate also confirms presidential nominees to key government positions, including federal judges and senior administration officials.If Democrats take control of either chamber, they could make it harder for Trump to pass legislation, influence budget negotiations and intensify congressional scrutiny of his administration through hearings and investigations.A Democratic majority in the House could also revive discussions of impeachment, although impeachment by itself would not remove the president from office. Removal requires a two-thirds vote in the Senate.Trump would remain president regardless of the election outcome. He would retain his executive powers and the ability to veto legislation, but a divided Congress could significantly constrain his domestic agenda.The cost of living, inflation, immigration and the economy are among the major concerns for voters. Foreign policy, including the war involving Iran, is also part of the political debate.Trump's approval ratings and public perceptions of his administration's performance are likely to influence the results. Midterm elections are often viewed as a referendum on the sitting president, with the party in the White House frequently losing congressional seats.Disputes over voting rules, election administration and the drawing of congressional district boundaries have also become contentious issues.Voting will take place on Tuesday, November 3, across the United States. Polling hours vary by state, and there is no single nationwide closing time.The first polling stations in parts of Indiana and Kentucky are scheduled to close at 6 pm Eastern Time, which is around 4.30 am on November 4 as per Indian Standard Time.Results are expected to emerge through the night, but close contests may take longer to resolve. Election officials must count outstanding ballots, verify results and, where necessary, conduct recounts or deal with legal challenges.News organisations may project winners before every ballot has been counted. Such projections are not official results. State election authorities certify the final results, a process that can take days or weeks.State election offices remain the primary source for official results, including vote counts, recounts and final certification.A close result can lead to recounts, court challenges and disputes over ballot validity. State officials handle the initial counting and certification process, but the US Constitution gives the House and Senate the power to judge the elections, returns and qualifications of their own members.A candidate or sitting member can challenge a congressional election result. In the House, such disputes are referred to the House Administration Committee, while Senate challenges go to the Senate Rules Committee. The respective chamber ultimately decides whether a member should be seated.This power could become significant if a handful of unresolved races determine which party controls Congress. Any House contests still unresolved when the new Congress convenes in January would be considered by the incoming House.The process can become politically contentious, particularly when party control is at stake. A disputed result may also leave a seat vacant while legal or congressional proceedings continue.
Article Summary: Voting will take place on Tuesday, November 3, across the United States. Polling stations in parts of Indiana and Kentucky are scheduled to close at 6pm. Results are expected to emerge through the night, but close contests may take longer to resolve.

Article Title: Dia Mirza's cracker-free Diwali appeal: HC expresses deep pain and displeasure; asks BMC to re-upload her video
Article Text:
Actor Dia Mirza

(With Agency Inputs)





MUMBAI: The Bombay high court has called the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation ’s (BMC) removal of actor Dia Mirza ’s video urging citizens to avoid firecrackers and noise pollution “unfortunate” and asked the civic body to restore it.“We would desire that in the event any goodwill message of any celebrity was taken off from the Corporation’s social media, it would be ideal if the same is put back in the spirit of what the Supreme Court observed that the festival is for everybody to celebrate. No person can be isolated from any festival being celebrated in this country,” the court observed.The HC, while taking up the suo motu PIL, hearing, said it was “disturbed at comments made by certain persons in regard to celebrities who had participated and assisted in public cause”.“The incident which has taken place yesterday, which in our opinion was unfortunate, was without taking into consideration the solemnity of the court orders and the whole intention and object of what was being sought to be achieved by spreading such awareness,” the court said.Reacting to the court's direction on the video of film actor Dia Mirza, UBT Shiv Sena MLA Aaditya Thackeray said, “The BJP makes every administration they take over into a circus! Total clownery in the BMC, where the mayor and her bosses claim they don’t know what the administration does whenever it goes wrong! Every other mayor globally is focussed on civic issues. Here, the mayor’s focus has been on her car’s red beacon, residence renovation and now a citizen’s religion in a video message that was asked for by the BMC itself!”National spokesperson for AIMIM Waris Pathan said, “The court has directed the BMC to re-upload Dia Mirza’s deleted video and also pulled up BJP leaders for their irrelevant criticism.The question remains: Why was Dia Mirza singled out when others made the same appeal? The issue was pollution and public health, not politics or someone’s surname.”BJP's Mumbai unit chief Ameet Satam on Monday linked appeals against the use of firecrackers during Diwali with the "tukde tukde gang", hours after the civic body removed actor Dia Mirza's video from its eco-friendly Diwali campaign following an objection raised by him.Satam alleged that anti-India forces were attempting to dictate how Hindus should celebrate the festival."Diwali has been celebrated for the last 5,000 years and will continue to be celebrated for thousands of years. We do not need to learn how to celebrate it from anyone. Members of the 'tukde tukde' gang and anti-India forces should not teach us how to celebrate Diwali," Satam said.Speaking to reporters, Satam alleged that certain elements in the country were joining hands with forces opposed to India and attempting to express sympathy towards those allegedly spreading anarchy.He also questioned the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) administration's decision to invite celebrities and make videos for its Diwali campaign, claiming the initiative was undertaken without consulting the BJP, which rules the civic body."Some celebrities had joined hands with anti-India forces and were attempting to sympathise with those spreading anarchy," he added.Mirza's video, in which she urged people to avoid noise and air pollution, was removed from the BMC's social media pages on Sunday. However, campaign videos featuring actors Madhuri Dixit and Nishigandha Wad, as well as cricketer Ajinkya Rahane, have been retained on the civic body's X and Instagram accounts.Earlier, hours after Satam raised the objection, the civic body, led by Municipal Commissioner Ashwini Bhide, removed Mirza's video from its social media pages, triggering a controversy.
Article Summary: The Bombay high court has called the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation’s removal of actor Dia Mirza ’s video ’unfortunate’ and asked the civic body to restore it. Mirza's video, in which she urged people to avoid noise and air pollution, was removed from the BMC's social media pages on Sunday.

Article Title: A Virginia couple turned their gravel backyard into a garden for their toddlers after buying a century-old home; a year later, neighbour claimed part of the land was his and demanded that fence be rem
Article Text:
Representative AI image

How a backyard makeover led to a dispute

Workers arrive to remove part of the fence

A judge intervenes in the boundary dispute

What the city and neighbouring owner have said

Why property surveys matter to homebuyers

A Virginia couple who transformed the gravel backyard of their century-old home into a garden for their two toddlers have found themselves caught in a property-boundary dispute after a neighbouring property owner claimed part of the land belonged to him. Brittany Ellerbe and her husband bought the house in Petersburg in 2025 and turned the outdoor space into a garden with grass, flowers and vegetable beds. About a year later, the dispute escalated when workers arrived to remove part of their fence at the request of the neighbouring property's seller. The couple challenged the move in court, and a judge subsequently ordered that the fence could not be removed or relocated while the legal dispute continued.When Brittany Ellerbe and her husband bought their home on South Dunlop Street in Petersburg, Virginia, the backyard was largely covered in gravel. The couple gradually transformed it into a garden, adding grass, fencing and vegetable beds where they grew flowers, zucchini, squash and bush beans.The garden also gave the family, which includes two toddlers, a private outdoor space. But the transformation became the centre of a dispute about a year after they purchased the property.According to a report by local broadcaster 12 On Your Side, a realtor representing the seller of a neighbouring house on Wilcox Street told Ellerbe that part of the backyard, including an area near the couple's steps, belonged to his client. The realtor reportedly said part of the fence would have to be removed so the neighbouring property could be sold.Ellerbe told 12 On Your Side that the couple received no further communication for months before the seller arrived with a truck carrying workers who began removing part of the fence.The couple subsequently received a letter from an attorney and a land survey showing boundary lines. Part of the removed fencing was reportedly used to enclose another section of the neighbouring property.The incident prompted the couple to seek legal help. Ellerbe said they had not received a physical survey, a deed or a letter from an attorney before the fence was removed.The dispute centres on whether the contested section of the backyard legally belongs to the couple or the neighbouring property owner. The available reporting has not established that either side has conclusively proved its claim.After hiring a lawyer, the couple obtained a court order in early October 2026. According to 12 On Your Side, a Petersburg judge granted an injunction and a temporary restraining order preventing the fence from being removed or moved until November 19, 2026.The order temporarily restricts further changes to the fence while the dispute proceeds. It does not constitute a final ruling on ownership of the disputed land.The case has raised questions about the property's historical records. Ellerbe told the broadcaster that the documents she had traced included an 1853 plat and a 1917 deed. She said she had struggled to find a recorded survey that clearly established the boundary.The judge reportedly raised concerns about missing records and whether the survey had been recorded. The underlying deeds, historic plats and survey would need to be examined to determine what they establish about the land.The Petersburg assessor's office told 12 On Your Side that the matter appeared to be a legal dispute between property owners.The broadcaster also visited the neighbouring property and left contact information for the homeowner but reported that it had not received a response by the time its report was published.As a result, the publicly available account contains more detail from Ellerbe's side than from the neighbouring owner's perspective. The legal dispute remains focused on the property boundary and the evidence available to establish ownership.The dispute highlights the importance of checking property boundaries when buying a home, particularly when fences, older deeds or historic land records are involved.Virginia's residential property disclosure guidance advises buyers to carry out their own due diligence because sellers do not make representations about current property lines. Buyers can seek information from local authorities and consider obtaining a property survey to help establish the boundaries of a parcel.A survey can provide important evidence, but a disagreement over ownership may also require examining deeds, historic plats and other legal records.
Article Summary: Brittany Ellerbe and her husband bought the house in Petersburg, Virginia, in 2025. They turned the gravel backyard into a garden with grass, flowers and vegetable beds. About a year later, the dispute escalated when workers arrived to remove part of their fence at the request of the neighbouring property's seller. The couple challenged the move in court, and a judge subsequently ordered that the fence could not be removed or relocated while the legal dispute continued.

Article Title: Bengaluru daylight robbery: How robber used Fevikwik to glue woman receptionist's hands to desk, held her at knifepoint and fled with Rs 4.5L gold chain- video
Article Text:
A masked robber stormed into a shoe and bag repair shop in Indiranagar, brandishing a knife and demanding valuables from the receptionist.





BENGALURU: A knife-wielding robber stormed into a shoe and bag repair shop in Indiranagar, threatened to kill a woman employee, attacked her and snatched her gold mangalya chain worth Rs 4.5 lakh in a daring daylight robbery on Oct 31.The accused, identified as Prabhuraj alias Raj, 40, had covered his head and face with a helmet and wore gloves. He also attacked the shop owner when he and members of the public tried to catch him before fleeing with the stolen chain.According to the complaint filed by Jayashree S, 23, a resident of Domlur, she has been working as a receptionist at Premium Shoe & Bag Repair on 100 Feet Road in Indiranagar for the past three years. The shop is owned by Ranjith Kumar. Her duties include receiving shoes and bags brought in by customers for repairs, issuing receipts and handing over the items to the workshop. She usually manages the shop's daily operations on her own.On Oct 31, Jayashree arrived at the shop around 10am and opened it for the day's work. Around 11.45am, an unidentified man wearing a helmet and gloves entered the shop. He suddenly jumped over the reception counter, where she was seated, and told her that someone was coming to kill him, warning her not to scream.Frightened, Jayashree tried to call Ranjith. However, Prabhuraj forcibly made her sit down, covered her mouth with his hands and pulled out a knife from his bag. He threatened to kill her if she raised an alarm and attacked her on the neck and hands with the knife.He then applied Fevikwik glue to both her hands to stick them to the desk and stuffed a piece of cloth lying on the desk into her mouth. He forcibly removed her gold mangalya chain, weighing around 35 grams and worth around Rs 4.5 lakh, from her neck and kept it in his pocket.When Prabhuraj attempted to flee, Jayashree managed to free her hands and screamed for help. Hearing her cries, members of the public rushed towards the shop. The accused then grabbed her by the hair, dragged her back inside and held a knife to her neck, warning those outside not to stop him.By then, Ranjith and others had reached the spot and tried to overpower him. Prabhuraj brandished the knife at them and attacked Ranjith before pulling Jayashree out of the shop and attempting to escape with the stolen chain.Members of the public and traffic police personnel present nearby chased the accused and caught him. Based on Jayashree's complaint, Indiranagar police registered a case under Section 309 (robbery) and arrested Prabhuraj.Deputy Commissioner of Police (East) Vikram Amathe said the woman was safe and had not sustained any injuries. He added that the accused appeared to be mentally disturbed and depressed. Police are verifying his background.
Article Summary: knife-wielding robber stormed into a shoe and bag repair shop in Indiranagar, brandishing a knife. He threatened to kill a woman employee, attacked her and snatched her gold mangalya chain worth Rs 4.5 lakh. The accused, identified as Prabhuraj alias Raj, 40, had covered his head and face with a helmet and wore gloves.
