A small city in Georgia is facing a police staffing crisis after its entire full-time police force resigned, with Mayor Craig Timmons confirming that he placed a GPS tracking device on the police chief's vehicle amid concerns over the officer's working hours.In an interview with WSB-TV's Channel 2 Action News, Timmons admitted that he had installed a tracking device on the truck driven by Milner Police Chief Lamar Bunn. He also confirmed placing a surveillance camera near a car wash, pointing towards City Hall, where the police chief's office is located.The mayor said his concerns were related to Bunn's timesheets, which required his signature. Timmons said he wanted to establish whether the chief was accurately accounting for his working hours.The admission comes after the chief, all five full-time police officers and most reserve personnel resigned, with their departures taking effect on October 28, 2026. The mass resignation has raised questions about the leadership of the department and how the city will maintain law enforcement services.Speaking to Channel 2 Action News, Timmons was directly asked whether he had placed a tracking device on the police vehicle used by Bunn."Yes, sir. I did," the mayor confirmed.He was also asked about a video camera installed near a car wash and pointed towards the building where the police chief's office is located. Timmons acknowledged that as well, saying it had been done with the property owner's approval.The mayor said he was responsible for signing off on the police chief's timesheets but had raised concerns about the working hours recorded. He also said he had prepared a report detailing allegations about Bunn's attendance records and use of city vehicles, which he planned to present at a special city council meeting.Timmons maintained that his responsibilities as mayor included overseeing the functioning of the city's administration.Bunn, however, has denied any wrongdoing. Speaking to the news channel by phone, he explained that his responsibilities as police chief were not restricted to working inside the police station or within the city's limits.He said he regularly handled administrative duties remotely, including responding to emails and monitoring police radio communications. He also maintained that his work continued beyond regular office hours."My job doesn't stop when I leave the office," Bunn said, explaining that he had even continued working while on vacation in Panama City.Assistant Chief Chris Landers also defended the department's working arrangements, saying it was common for officers to work outside the city and receive calls after regular working hours.Bunn's position was that his work responsibilities extended beyond a fixed workplace and schedule.The controversy has unfolded against the backdrop of an unprecedented staffing crisis for Milner. The chief and all five full-time officers submitted their resignations, with the departures taking effect on October 28. Most reserve personnel also reportedly left the department.A resignation letter obtained by WSB-TV cited concerns about the "judgment and decision-making" of the mayor and certain city council members regarding the police department.The tracking device was among the issues that reportedly contributed to the officers' concerns. An officer who spoke to the news channel also pointed to restrictions on opportunities to take up off-duty jobs as a possible factor.Timmons, however, said there had been a miscommunication over the issue and maintained that neither he nor the city council had issued an order restricting officers from taking such work.Bunn also said he had not asked the officers to resign.With Milner's full-time police department no longer operational, Lamar County Sheriff Brad White said his deputies would continue responding to calls in the city, as they had previously done.He indicated that if the absence of a local police department continued for an extended period, Milner would need to enter into a formal arrangement with the sheriff's office for police services.Timmons said he remained confident that the city would be able to rebuild its police department. He also claimed that he had already started receiving unsolicited applications from people interested in police positions, as well as the city manager's role.City Manager Tausha Grose also resigned shortly after the police department's mass departure, according to local reports.During the interview, Timmons defended his actions and spoke about his personal journey, including his recovery from drug addiction and his religious faith."Right is right and wrong is wrong," he said, adding that he had turned his life over to Jesus 15 years ago and had made a promise to do right by the people he encountered.The situation has left the small Georgia city dealing with more than a dispute over a police chief's timesheets. With its full-time officers gone, Milner now faces the challenge of restoring its police department while addressing the concerns about leadership and trust that surfaced in the resignation letters.
Article Summary: Mayor Craig Timmons admitted placing a GPS tracking device on the truck driven by Milner Police Chief Lamar Bunn. He also confirmed placing a surveillance camera near a car wash, pointing towards City Hall, where the police chief's office is located. Timmons said he wanted to establish whether the chief was accurately accounting for his working hours. Bunn has denied any wrongdoing, saying his work responsibilities extended beyond a fixed workplace and schedule.

Article Title: A Louisiana man died without a will in 1956, and a 1996 court order named his daughter as heir to half a property; 30 years later, the state Supreme Court blocked a rival family's attempt to undo that
Article Text:
Louisiana SC blocks a family's challenge to 1996 ruling granting a daughter half her father's property. (AI image)

How the property dispute began

Why rival family challenged inheritance

Why Supreme Court rejected the challenge

A property dispute involving a Louisiana man who died without leaving a will in 1956 has reached the state's Supreme Court, nearly 30 years after a court recognised his daughter as the heir to his estate. In a ruling delivered on October 30, the Louisiana Supreme Court blocked an attempt by another family to overturn the 1996 inheritance decision. The judges ruled that the challenge had been brought too late under state law, leaving the earlier decision recognising Earnestine Walker's inheritance rights intact.According to the judgement , the dispute concerned a piece of land in DeSoto Parish, Louisiana, where two families claimed ownership through different records dating back several decades. At the centre of the disagreement was Augustine Howard's 50% share of the property, known in court documents as Tract 2.The case began as a disagreement over who owned the land but eventually turned into a legal challenge to a court order issued in 1996. That order had recognised Walker as Howard's sole heir. The opposing family argued that she should not have inherited the property under the law that existed when her father died.The Supreme Court did not examine whether Walker was entitled to inherit the property under the law in place at the time. Instead, it considered whether the rival claimants could legally challenge the 1996 ruling nearly three decades later. The court overturned the rulings of two lower courts and sent the case back for further proceedings.The property's ownership history goes back to 1924, when Tract 2 was divided between Augustine Howard and Inez Howard. Each received a 50% ownership interest.Howard died in 1956 without a will. Four decades later, a court issued a judgment recognising Earnestine Walker as the sole heir to his estate. Windward Land, LLC and Michael Morris Gulley later claimed an interest in the property through Walker's ownership rights.However, another group, identified in the judgment as the Frazier-Edwards respondents, claimed ownership through Addie Edwards. Their claim was connected to a 1955 deed executed by Zephyr Johnson, who was Inez Howard's daughter and Augustine Howard's niece.The competing claims became part of a lawsuit filed by Windward Land and Gulley seeking to divide the property among its owners.During those proceedings, the Frazier-Edwards family challenged the 1996 inheritance order. They argued that Walker, described in the court documents as a child born outside marriage, could not legally have inherited Howard's estate under the law applicable in 1956.The family's argument relied on an earlier Louisiana inheritance law that treated children born outside marriage differently from those born within marriage.Under the law in force between 1908 and 1981, a child born outside marriage could not inherit from a parent who died without a will if that parent had children legally recognised as born within marriage.Although the provision was later declared unconstitutional, the court ruling striking it down was made retroactive only to January 1, 1975. Howard had died in 1956.The Frazier-Edwards respondents therefore argued that Walker should never have been recognised as his heir.The trial court accepted their argument and declared the 1996 inheritance judgment ineffective. It instead recognised Zephyr Johnson as Howard's rightful heir, leading to a ruling that the Frazier-Edwards respondents owned the entire property.Windward challenged that decision, arguing that the family had waited far beyond the legally permitted period to question the inheritance order.The trial court rejected Windward's request for a new trial, and an appeals court subsequently upheld the earlier decision. Windward then approached the Louisiana Supreme Court.The Supreme Court examined Louisiana Revised Statute 9:5630, which generally provides a two-year deadline for certain inheritance-related claims involving property acquired from a person recognised as an heir.The disagreement concerned who was covered by that deadline. The Frazier-Edwards respondents argued that the restriction applied only to heirs or beneficiaries directly claiming inheritance rights from the deceased person. They maintained that their claim, based on property transferred through Addie Edwards, was different. The Supreme Court disagreed.Justice Griffin, writing for the court, explained that the term "successor" was not limited to someone directly inheriting property. It could also include buyers, people receiving property as gifts and others who obtained ownership rights through transfers.The judges concluded that the Frazier-Edwards respondents were also covered by the two-year deadline. Their attempt to invalidate the 1996 judgment was therefore legally barred.The court also warned that allowing people to avoid the deadline simply by transferring property to someone else would undermine the purpose of the law, which is to provide certainty over ownership.The Supreme Court thus ruled that the 1996 inheritance judgment remained valid and had transferred Augustine Howard's 50% interest in Tract 2 to Earnestine Walker. It overturned the lower courts' decisions and returned the case to the trial court for further proceedings.
Article Summary: Louisiana Supreme Court blocks challenge to 1996 ruling granting a daughter half her father's property. The judges ruled that the challenge had been brought too late under state law. The dispute concerned a piece of land in DeSoto Parish, Louisiana, where two families claimed ownership through different records dating back decades.

Article Title: A Delaware couple cared for a backyard triangle for over 20 years before neighbours demanded $30,000 to let them keep the fenced land; an October 30 court ruling has now awarded the entire disputed st
Article Text:
Decades of maintenance establishing continuous control

Failed negotiations and monetary demands

Division of the disputed triangular parcel

A long-running property dispute between neighbours in Newark, Delaware, has ended with a court ruling that gives homeowners legal ownership of a piece of land they had looked after for more than 20 years. According to legal documents published by Justia Law, the Delaware Court of Chancery issued a decision in an adverse possession case involving Plaintiffs Joseph W.C. Murray, Jr. and Danielle F. Murray and Defendants Nikola Preradovic, Rade Preradovic, and Zeljka Preradovic. The dispute involved a triangular piece of land along the boundary between two neighbouring homes in New Castle County. The Murrays showed that they had openly, continuously, and exclusively used the enclosed rear part of the disputed land for more than the 20 years required under Delaware law. As a result, the court awarded them full legal ownership of that section.Court records show that the Murrays had looked after the fenced section of land for around 25 years. The family put up fences, maintained the garden, and regularly treated the rear area behind their home as part of their own yard. Over the years, the Murrays placed several personal items inside the fenced area. These included a stone retaining wall, garden features, a beehive, and a decorative statue.Photographs and witness statements presented in court showed that these items had remained there over time. This helped confirm that the family had continued to control and use the rear yard without interruption. Under Delaware property laws, anyone claiming land through adverse possession must prove that their use of the property was open, visible, continuous, exclusive, and against the interests of the legal owner for at least 20 years. The court explained that continuous use does not mean someone must be physically present every minute. Instead, they must act like an owner in a way that suits the type of land involved.The legal dispute began after the Preradovic family bought the neighbouring property at 234 South Dilwyn in December 2022. Soon after buying the property, the new owners noticed differences in the boundary lines after land surveys. They asked the Murrays to move or remove the existing fence. During the first discussions, both sides considered officially changing the property boundaries through New Castle County authorities. However, the talks broke down because they could not agree on the financial terms. Court documents show that the new property owners asked the Murrays to pay $30,000 in exchange for signing a deed transfer that would allow them to keep the fenced land. The Murrays refused to pay and claimed they already had rights to the land because they had used it for many years. The disagreement then led to a formal case in the Court of Chancery. At first, the Murrays asked the court to enforce what they said was an agreement to transfer the land. In an earlier decision, Magistrate in Chancery Loren Mitchell found that the claimed sale agreement could not be legally enforced. This was because both sides had not clearly agreed on the exact legal description of the property. The case then moved forward to a full review of the main adverse possession claim.When reviewing the land and its layout, the Court of Chancery divided the disputed triangular area into three separate sections. These were the enclosed rear yard behind the fence, a stone planter area, and an unfenced grass lawn stretching towards the street. The court decided that the Murrays had met all the legal requirements for adverse possession of the rear section enclosed by the fence and retaining wall. The ruling explained that the fence clearly showed that the family was treating the land as their own. This would have been obvious to anyone who owned or lived on the neighbouring property. However, the court rejected the Murrays' claim to the front sections of the triangular plot. These included the planter area and the front grass strip beside the road. The court found that the family had not maintained these areas regularly. There were periods when the grass became overgrown, and other people also had access to the space. The judge ruled that regularly cutting grass along an unfenced front boundary was not enough to prove exclusive control against the legal owner. Such activity did not meet the legal standard needed to take ownership away from someone who already held the deed. As a result, the court officially awarded the Murrays ownership of the enclosed rear yard. However, the Preradovic family kept legal ownership of the outer front lawn. The decision therefore settled the central boundary dispute while making clear that long-term use alone does not guarantee ownership unless all the legal requirements for adverse possession are met.
Article Summary: The dispute involved a triangular piece of land along the boundary between two neighbouring homes in New Castle County, Delaware. The Murrays showed that they had openly, continuously, and exclusively used the enclosed rear part of the disputed land for more than the 20 years required under Delaware law. As a result, the court awarded them full legal ownership of that section.

Article Title: Who was Erin Benavides? Revisiting her connection to Tony Parker and Eva Longoria after tragic news
Article Text:
Erin Benavides and Tony Parker. Image via: Pure Flats / Facebook | Getty

Erin Benavides and her alleged link to Tony Parker

Erin Benavides. Image via: Christina Mitchell / Facebook

Erin Benavides’ career and work for children

Erin Benavides, a former Texas prosecutor once at the center of an NBA scandal, has died by suicide at 54. According to TMZ, Police found her dead at a home in Port Aransas on Oct. 14 after a friend of her husband alerted them to a worrying text message she had sent. The news came out this week and brought fresh attention to the 2010 claims linking her to Spurs star Tony Parker, who was married to actress Eva Longoria at the time. Benavides denied the affair. The investigation is still open, and police do not suspect foul play.Benavides first made national headlines in 2010. She was married to Brent Barry then, who was Parker’s Spurs teammate from 2004 to 2008. Barry divorced her and alleged an emotional affair with the six-time All-Star. Longoria reportedly found hundreds of text messages from another woman on his phone, later identified as Benavides. Benavides denied the affair, and Parker reportedly denied any physical contact.Both marriages ended. Benavides and Barry had been married since 1998 and split in 2010. Longoria filed for divorce in November of that year, and the two divorced in 2011. The actress later told Extra that Parker had also cheated earlier in their marriage.Benavides later built a career in law. She worked as an assistant district attorney in Texas’ 38th Judicial District, which covers Uvalde and Real counties, from January 2023 until she resigned in August 2026. Her work was in the anti-gang and border prosecution unit.Outside the courtroom, she focused on children. From 2020 to 2022, she was president and CEO of the Youth Center of Texas, which offers crisis intervention and case management to child sex-trafficking victims. Yolanda Valenzuela, executive director of Kym’s Angels Foundation, also recalled her work with the Bexar County Child Welfare Board, where she helped run mass-adoption ceremonies and a Christmas fundraiser that bought gifts for local foster children.District Attorney Christina Mitchell paid tribute on Facebook. Mitchell said Benavides brought laughter and energy to the office and often spoke with pride about her sons. “Her boisterous laugh throughout the office will be greatly missed,” Mitchell wrote. She added that Benavides would be remembered for her dedication to the border unit and to making both counties safer.If you or someone you know is struggling with suicidal thoughts or emotional distress, call or text 988 for 24/7 support, or visit 988lifeline.org for help.
Article Summary: Erin Benavides, a former Texas prosecutor once at the center of an NBA scandal, has died by suicide at 54. Police found her dead at a home in Port Aransas on Oct. 14 after a friend of her husband alerted them to a worrying text message she had sent. The news brought fresh attention to the 2010 claims linking her to Spurs star Tony Parker, who was married to actress Eva Longoria at the time.

Article Title: Princess Catherine’s sister Pippa Middleton and husband James Matthews ordered to demolish unauthorised car park at £15.5 million estate; neighbours raise concerns over construction without consultati
Article Text:
Pippa Middleton and James Matthews have faced criticism from locals over construction and public access to their estate. (Photo: Instagram/Google Maps)

Council rules car park development was visually intrusive

Neighbours objected to construction without consultation

Pippa Middleton and husband James Matthews have been ordered to demolish an unauthorised car park at their £15.5 million estate. (Photo: Instagram)

Pippa Middleton and James Matthews' previous dispute with locals

Pippa Middleton and her hedge fund manager husband, James Matthews, have been ordered to remove a car park they built on their sprawling country estate without obtaining prior planning permission. The decision comes after a group of residents in the picturesque village of Kintbury raised objections with West Berkshire Council, claiming they had not been consulted before construction began last year.Pippa, the younger sister of Princess Catherine, and James own the land, which forms part of their £15.5 million, 145-acre Barton Court estate. The couple moved into the property in 2022 and have since been involved in several disagreements with locals over developments and access to the estate.According to a report by The Times, the couple subsequently applied for retrospective planning permission for the anglers' car park, arguing that the sale of fishing rights along the River Kennet was a significant source of income that helped support the upkeep of the estate.However, West Berkshire Council rejected the proposal, concluding that the development was 'visually intrusive and urbanised' and had 'eroded a measure of the open and undeveloped rural character' of the North Wessex Downs.The couple have now been directed to remove the car park.The development reportedly involved covering around 400 square metres of meadow with a hard surface for agricultural use. Before the property changed ownership, the land had been used for grazing by two heavy horses, Monty and Drummer, which were familiar to local residents.The car park drew considerable criticism from residents, who approached the council after noticing the construction. In objections submitted to the authorities, locals said they were 'shocked' by the development and questioned why the community had not been consulted before work began.Some residents also alleged that the car park had been created to move vehicles away from areas closer to the couple's home, thereby preserving the views around their property.One objector reportedly wrote: 'This application is to move unsightly parking out of sight of the applicants on entry to the Barton Court estate to the detriment of the residents and the heritage of Kintbury.'Another resident highlighted concerns about the location, traffic congestion and the potential impact on the area's heritage, requesting that the planning committee conduct a site inspection before reaching a decision.Planners also raised concerns about the absence of mitigation measures to protect the River Kennet from potential adverse environmental impacts.This is not the first time Pippa and James have faced opposition from local residents since moving to Barton Court. The couple had earlier drawn criticism for restricting public access to Mill Lane, a route running through their estate that had reportedly been used by dog walkers and ramblers for years.The Grade I-listed Barton Court, located along the River Kennet near Kintbury, was previously owned by the late retail tycoon Sir Terence Conran, who had permitted members of the public to use the lane.However, after Pippa and James moved into the property with their three children, Arthur, Grace and Rose, in 2022, they installed an electric gate to restrict access. Signs reading 'Private: No Public Access' and 'No Trespassing' also appeared around the estate.The move prompted 35 residents, supported by the Ramblers Association, to approach West Berkshire Council, seeking to have Mill Lane officially recognised as a public right of way.A Planning Inspectorate inquiry into the dispute began at the village hall in May. James Matthews also attended the proceedings, where he reportedly argued that the family's security and privacy concerns should be taken into consideration.
Article Summary: Council rules car park development was visually intrusive and urbanised. Neighbours objected to construction without consultation with council. Couple moved into the property in 2022 and have since been involved in several disagreements with locals over developments and access to the estate.

Article Title: ‘Cause of blaze, extent of loss yet to be determined’: Luthra brothers, partner to pay 20L to each of 25 Birch fire victims' kin
Article Text:
Being G S Hospitality Goa Arpora LLP has committed to provide Rs 20 lakh ex-gratia compensation for each victim.





PANAJI: Bombay high court on Monday recorded the statement of Being G S Hospitality Goa Arpora LLP, whose partners include Saurabh and Gaurav Luthra and Ajay Gupta, that it will deposit ex-gratia compensation of Rs 20 lakh for the family of each of the 25 victims of the Birch by Romeo Lane nightclub fire tragedy.The victims include 20 employees and five tourists who died in the fire at the nightclub.The court recorded the statement of the LLP that it will deposit the first instalment of Rs 5 lakh for each victim by Nov 16, the second instalment of Rs 5 lakh by Dec 7, and the remaining Rs 10 lakh by Feb 7. This will be over and above the Rs 2 lakh ex-gratia compensation already paid by the LLP to the families of the 20 deceased employees.The bench of Justices Valmiki Menezes and Amit Jamsandekar said the amount deposited will be adjusted against any final compensation orders passed in proceedings pending before the labour commissioner under the Workmen's Compensation Act concerning the 20 deceased employees, as well as proceedings initiated by the families of the deceased tourists before the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Gurugram, Haryana.According to Haldankar, eight fire tenders from Kundaim, Ponda, Old Goa, Margao, Bicholim and St Inez-Panaji headquarters were pressed into service. Firefighters made repeated trips to spray around 1.7 lakh litres of water and used about 700 litres of foam to bring the blaze under control.“Considering the intensity of fire engulfing plastic and rubber waste we had to spray around 700 litres of foam to douse the fire,” Haldankar said.He said firefighters had contained the blaze by morning, but isolated fires continued to flare up.Heavy earthmoving machinery was deployed to sift through the scrap, move debris and cover isolated hotspots and embers with mud.“We have engaged earth machinery to sift the garbage,” a fire official said.Toxic smoke billowed from the site, hampering firefighting operations.An LPG cylinder was found inside the shed, where some labourers were staying. No injuries were reported.Fire officials said the cause of the blaze had not yet been determined.“We have not found the cause. When we reached here, the fire was everywhere. There is plastic, wires and paper, cardboard and cables that have been dumped here. All this creates a lot of smoke. We are not sure about the loss but to us all this looks like scrap. We used 1.7 lakh litres of water to douse the fire and the smoke still keeps coming,” a firefighter said.A person residing near the site alleged that the scrapyard was operating without permission from the panchayat. The fire and emergency services director visited the site, while police and revenue department officials also conducted inquiries.Santosh Naik, who claimed to be the owner of the land where the scrapyard was operating, said he had sought to evict the operator from the plot.“I found out about the fire in the morning. This scrapyard has been working for three years. We had asked the operator to remove the scrap. We had written to the collector and a case is being heard by the collector. We gave the land to the operator but not for scrap,” Naik said.
Article Summary: Being G S Hospitality Goa Arpora LLP has committed to provide Rs 20 lakh ex- gratia compensation for each victim. The victims include 20 employees and five tourists who died in the fire at the nightclub. The amount will be adjusted against any final compensation orders passed in proceedings pending before the labour commissioner.

Article Title: Cyclone Murasu crosses Andhra coast with 120 kmph gusts, triggers heavy rain, damages in coastal districts
Article Text:
The maximum peak surge is expected over Bapatla, as well as Krishna and Prakasam districts.





VISAKHAPATNAM: The severe cyclonic storm Murasu moved north-northwestwards and crossed the south Andhra Pradesh coast between Nellore and Narsapur, close to Ongole, between 3.30 am and 5.30 am on Tuesday, with wind speeds of 100-110 kmph, gusting to 120 kmph.The cyclone triggered heavy to extremely heavy rainfall, uprooted trees and electric poles, caused power outages and communication disruptions, and damaged roads in parts of Prakasam, Palnadu, Bapatla and Guntur districts of Andhra Pradesh, as well as other parts of the state.Heavy spells of rainfall are likely to continue over south coastal Andhra Pradesh till Tuesday evening.Kothapatnam in Prakasam district recorded 16.4 cm of rainfall between 8.30 am on Monday and 5 am on Tuesday, followed by 11.4 cm in Naguluppalapadu (Prakasam), 10 cm in Chirala (Bapatla), 9.3 cm in Pelluru (Prakasam), 9.2 cm in Throvagunta (Prakasam), 8.5 cm each in ANGR Agriculture College (Bapatla) and Santhanuthlapdu (Prakasam), 8 cm in Bapatla, 7.9 cm in Mogallthur (West Godavari), 7.7 cm in Pakala (Prakasam), 7.5 cm in Chilakapdu (Prakasam) and 7.4 cm in Malikipuram (Konaseema).The weather system is likely to move north-northwestwards and gradually weaken into a cyclonic storm, with wind speeds reaching 80-90 kmph and gusting to 100 kmph, by Tuesday afternoon. It is likely to further weaken into a deep depression, with wind speeds reaching 55-65 kmph and gusting to 75 kmph, by midnight on Tuesday.A storm surge of about 1.0-1.5 metres above the astronomical tide is very likely to inundate low-lying areas of south coastal Andhra Pradesh in the next few hours. The maximum peak surge is expected over Bapatla, as well as Krishna and Prakasam districts. It is likely to gradually decrease thereafter, becoming less than 0.5 metres by noon.
Article Summary: The severe cyclonic storm Murasu moved north-northwestwards and crossed the south Andhra Pradesh coast between Nellore and Narsapur. The cyclone triggered heavy to extremely heavy rainfall, uprooted trees and caused power outages and communication disruptions.

Article Title: HPCL's Visakhapatnam refinery hit by major fire near oil tank; explosion reports under scrutiny
Article Text:
The flames reportedly erupted near a tank containing Ruf Pitch Oil and rose to considerable heights, attracting the attention of people travelling along adjoining roads.





VISAKHAPATNAM: A massive fire broke out at Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Ltd's (HPCL) Visakh Refinery on Monday evening, triggering panic in the surrounding industrial areas of Malkapuram and Sriharipuram.The flames reportedly erupted near a tank containing Ruf Pitch Oil and rose to considerable heights, attracting the attention of people travelling along adjoining roads.Several commuters recorded videos of the incident on their mobile phones. The videos subsequently went viral on social media, causing anxiety among residents in the vicinity.According to preliminary information from HPCL sources, no injuries or casualties were reported. The exact cause of the fire is yet to be established.Rumours of an explosion in the oil tank spread across the industrial area. However, HPCL sources indicated that the possibility of a tank explosion was considered low. Officials were examining the circumstances that led to the fire.Ruf Pitch Oil is an intermediate product used in the manufacture of bitumen.
Article Summary: The flames reportedly erupted near a tank containing Ruf Pitch Oil. No injuries or casualties were reported. The exact cause of the fire is yet to be established. Rumours of an explosion in the oil tank spread across the industrial area. However, HPCL sources indicated that the possibility of a tank explosion was considered low.

Article Title: Day after cops’ protest at police headquarters, Delhi ACP Manasvi Vashistha receives suspension letter
Article Text:
Assistant commissioner of police Manasvi Vashistha was suspended after protests by Delhi Police personnel regarding their officer transfers

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you agree with the suspension of ACP Manasvi Vashistha following the protest? Yes, it was justified No, it was not justified 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





NEW DELHI: Hours after leading a protest outside and inside Police Headquarters, assistant commissioner of police (ACP) Manasvi Vashistha was suspended by the ministry of home affairs (MHA).Police sources said Vashistha has received his suspension letter.The development comes a day after hundreds of Delhi Police personnel gathered at police headquarters (PHQ) to protest the transfer of Vashistha and inspector Arun Kumar after a confrontation between police personnel and lawyers at Shahdara police station on October 23.Delhi Police, however, described the gathering as a ‘sampark sabha’ (interaction).The transfers followed an alleged scuffle in which an advocate sustained a serious head injury.Lawyers accused the two officers of misbehaviour and alleged that the ACP had brandished his pistol. Vashistha, previously posted in Gandhi Nagar, was transferred to the Special Police Unit for Women and Children (SPUWAC), while Shahdara SHO Kumar was moved to the security unit.Vashistha, whose transfer triggered the demonstration, led the protest. Personnel circulated messages in WhatsApp groups urging them to assemble at PHQ.He also posted a video appealing to police commissioner Anurag Kumar for an open-house discussion.The demonstration unfolded in two phases, outside the headquarters and later inside. Around 100 personnel initially gathered outside PHQ, but the number grew to about 500 when the meeting was called.Security was strengthened, with additional police and CAPF personnel deployed near Gate No. 1 and barricades erected.Several videos surfaced showing senior officers attempting to dissuade personnel from gathering. In one, DCP (New Delhi) Sachin Sharma reminded them that they belonged to a professional and disciplined force and should raise their concerns through departmental channels.Speaking to reporters, Vashistha said the mobilisation was an organic call by police personnel and that he had joined it.He said a formal application had been submitted seeking a platform to present their grievances before senior officers.Addressing the gathering, the ACP called for a clear standard operating procedure (SOP) to deal with lawyers entering police stations.He said the entry of more than five people wearing black coats should be treated as an unlawful assembly. He also demanded a dedicated cell at PHQ to address such incidents, immediate cancellation of bar licences in cases of misbehaviour with police personnel and the deployment of two companies of security forces at every court complex.Protesters were seen holding placards featuring photographs of two retired IPS officers and ACP Vashistha. The placards read, “Our Heroes Forever.”A similar demonstration was organised in November 2019 following clashes between police personnel and lawyers at Tis Hazari Court.A protesting policeman said the Bar Council could not dictate terms to Delhi Police personnel, adding that they would fight for respect in a disciplined and peaceful manner.He also said police personnel should not be intimidated in courts, where they play an important role in the judicial process. Another policeman said they faced harassment from lawyers on court premises.A meeting was subsequently held at Vimarsh Hall, attended by the police commissioner and senior officers. Personnel raised concerns over the dignity of the force, respect for the uniform and the need for a structured grievance-redressal mechanism.According to an official press note, the commissioner appreciated the force’s professionalism and commitment, particularly during law-and-order duties and the BRICS Summit, and assured prompt action on genuine grievances.Delhi Police also announced the formation of a joint coordination committee comprising representatives of bar associations and the Bar Council of Delhi at district and PHQ levels to address issues faced by personnel while performing their duties.Matters relating to promotions, MACP, housing and other service-related concerns will also be examined. District and unit heads have been directed to hold regular meetings and ensure time-bound resolution of grievances under the supervision of senior officers.After the meeting, which lasted more than 40 minutes, several policemen returned to the road outside PHQ, with about 40 continuing their protest.
Article Summary: Assistant commissioner of police (ACP) Manasvi Vashistha was suspended by the ministry of home affairs (MHA) The development comes a day after hundreds of Delhi Police personnel gathered at police headquarters (PHQ) to protest the transfer of the ACP and inspector Arun Kumar. The transfers followed an alleged scuffle in which an advocate sustained a serious head injury.

Article Title: Ahmedabad hit-and-run: Speeding Fortuner runs over family of 3 sleeping on footpath; woman dies
Article Text:
A woman was killed when a speeding Toyota Fortuner ran over a family sleeping on a footpath





AHMEDABAD: A woman was killed and two others were seriously injured after a speeding Toyota Fortuner ran over a family sleeping on a footpath near Devashya School in Nikol. The driver abandoned the SUV and fled, but was later caught by police.A beer can was found inside the vehicle, registered in the name of Viral Chaudhary, a resident of Mansa. Police have not disclosed the identity of the driver.The three victims were taken to a hospital, where the woman succumbed to her injuries.DCP (Traffic-East) Naresh Kanjharia said, “We are checking whether the driver had consumed intoxicants.”Police have registered an offence against the driver.Residents said speeding and late-night racing were frequent in the area and alleged that police had failed to curb the menace. They also claimed that liquor was sold openly in the locality, but police rarely acted against those involved.Inspector SI Sumra of the I Division traffic police, under whose jurisdiction the accident occurred, could not be reached for comment despite repeated attempts.The accident comes amid concerns over drunk driving in the city. In Sept, police constable Gaurang Baldevbhai Dave, posted at the Naroda police station, was arrested after his SUV allegedly rammed a scooter near Sapteshwar Mahadev Temple in Chandkheda.The collision seriously injured a pharmacist and his 15-year-old niece. Dave was accused of driving under the influence of alcohol.In March, a 22-year-old driver allegedly under the influence of alcohol rammed his speeding car into a taxi and another parked car near Vastrapur lake, injuring two people.
Article Summary: A woman was killed and two others were seriously injured after a Toyota Fortuner ran over a family sleeping on a footpath. The driver abandoned the SUV and fled, but was later caught by police. A beer can was found inside the vehicle, registered in the name of Viral Chaudhary, a resident of Mansa.

Article Title: Lured through Instagram, killed over love triangle? Keralam teen found stuffed in sack, 3 held
Article Text:
Abhiram MD, a 16-year-old student, was reported missing and later found dead in a sack (R: AI-generated image used for representational purposes)





THIRUVANANTHAPURAM: Abhiram MD, 16, a class XI student of NSS HSS Paruthippara who was reported missing from his home in Sreekaryam on Sunday, was allegedly murdered, with police locating his body inside a sack that was abandoned in a vacant plot at Pangappara.City commissioner Arul RB Krishna said that three persons, including a minor girl, were taken into custody in connection with the case.A 17-year-old boy and Sreekaryam resident Ummar, who is also on the police goon list, allegedly initiated the crime.Both confessed to the crime, he said, adding that the girl's role in the crime will become clear as the investigation progresses.Preliminary probe indicated that a dispute allegedly linked to his friendship with a girl may have led to the murder.The police suspect that the accused used the girl's Instagram account to lure him to an isolated location. Investigators believe Abhiram was strangled using a belt and his body was subsequently stuffed inside a sack and abandoned at the vacant plot.The minor is suspected to have been close to the girl, while investigators are examining whether Abhiram's interaction with her had triggered a dispute between the boys.Abhiram had left his home around 3pm on Sunday, telling his family that he was going to Pangappara to meet friends. His relatives said he had received a phone call just before he left his home.He later called his father and reportedly said that he would return home soon. However, when he failed to return home by evening, his family organized a search to locate him. Repeated attempts to contact him proved unsuccessful as his mobile phone was switched off.The family subsequently approached Sreekaryam Police and lodged a missing-person complaint.The police launched an investigation using the boy's mobile phone details and expanded the probe to his circle of friends. Investigators examined CCTV footage, phone and tower location details, which eventually helped them trace the sequence of events and locate the body at Pangappara.The family said Abhiram appeared normal and did not exhibit signs of anxiety or depression before he left his home.Relatives alleged that there was a delay in tracing Abhiram after they approached the police. Police are ascertaining whether more people were involved in the crime.The suspects are being questioned now and inquest has been completed.The body was shifted to Thiruvananthapuram Medical College for autopsy.
Article Summary: Abhiram MD, 16, a class XI student of NSS HSS Paruthippara, was reported missing from his home in Sreekaryam on Sunday. Police locating his body inside a sack that was abandoned in a vacant plot at Pangappara. Three persons, including a minor girl, were taken into custody in connection with the case.

Article Title: Heads smashed in, throats slit with knife: Steeped in debt, Bhopal man kills mother, wife, 2 kids in sleep, then dies by suicide
Article Text:
The house in Chhola area where the gruesome murders took place

Seen in CCTV leaving home

Chilling last call

Door broken, bodies recovered





BHOPAL: Suspected mental stress over unpaid debts triggered a macabre chain of killings, after a 35-year-old former restaurateur allegedly pounded the heads of his mother, wife and two children with a hammer before slashing their throats at their rented house in Bhopal’s Chhola police station area on Monday, before jumping in front of a speeding train.The horrifying events unfolded at PMAY LIG Colony of Malikhedi, near Titori Ghat of Chhola police station area, police said, adding that initial suspicions indicate running unpaid debt and mounting fiscal distress possibly drove him to commit the gory murders, though the motive remains undetermined.The 35-year-old was identified as Narendra Sahu, police said, adding that he locked the main door from outside after killing his loved ones before proceeding towards Chopda Kalan in the Sukhi Sewania police station area where jumped to his death before an on-rushing train.The deceased were identified as Narendra’s mother Saraswati, 55, his wife Somlata, 30, daughter Kirti, 10, and son Kush, 6, police said, adding that from an initial survey of the crime scene it appeared as though their heads were smashed with a hammer before their throats were slit with a knife.According to the first police responders, Somlata and Kush were found lying in a pool of blood on the bed in one room, while Saraswati and Kirti were found lifeless on the bed in a separate room of the rented tenement.Police recovered the blood-stained hammer and knife from the house, adding that there were no visible signs of a struggle, indicating that the family members were killed while they were asleep in the wee hours of Monday.According to investigators, the possibility that Narendra may have drugged or poisoned his victims, leaving them unable to resist his murderous blows, wasn’t being ruled out at this stage of the probe.Small glass bottles found in the kitchen during the initial sweep of the crime scene were sent for forensic examination, while traces of blood were detected in the wash basin, suggesting Narendra may have washed his bloodied hands clean before leaving the house.Investigators mined footage from a CCTV camera installed at the colony, showing Narendra motoring away in his 350cc Bullet after locking the door from outside.His headless remains were found on the railway tracks at Chopda Kalan around 10am, while his motorcycle was parked nearby. His mobile phone and the house key were recovered from his person.Narendra rang up his brother-in-law, Deepak Singh, who also resides in Chhola area, minutes before he jumped to his death, asking him to reach Chopda Kalan at the earliest, police said, adding that when Deepak asked why, the former said it was urgent before the call went cold.Deepak reached the village as told but could not contact Narendra despite repeated calls. He then returned to Narendra’s house and, finding it locked, tried calling Somlata. But she did not answer either. He assumed the family was travelling and unavailable to take calls.Meanwhile, Sukhi Sewania police received information around 10am that a man was found dead on the railway tracks. Police recovered Narendra’s last remains, along with his motorcycle and mobile phone and got in touch with Deepak after poring over his call records.Deepak identified the deceased as Narendra and subsequently returned to the rented house around 1pm.With repeated calls to the family still going unanswered, Deepak sensed trouble and contacted Chhola police on Dial-112, reporting that there was information on the whereabouts of his family.Responding to Deepak’s call, a Chhola police team reached the Malikhedi residence and broke open the main door lock. The four family members were found dead in two rooms, bringing the disturbing murders to light.Senior police officers, including DCP (Zone-4) Adarshkant Shukla, reached the spot along with an FSL team.The hammer and knife, the suspected murder weapons, were found lying in the kitchen, the sleuths said, adding that no suicide note was found. Narendra’s mobile phone has been seized for further forensic analysis.DCP Shukla said a case of unnatural death was registered in connection with the incident, adding that an FIR for murder would be filed soon.
Article Summary: Narendra Sahu, 35, allegedly pounded the heads of his mother, wife and two children with a hammer before slashing their throats at their rented house in Bhopal’s Chhola police station area. Initial suspicions indicate running unpaid debt and mounting fiscal distress possibly drove him to commit the gory murders, though the motive remains undetermined.

Article Title: Liquor smuggler runs over cop in Madhya Pradesh district where hooch killed 12
Article Text:
The truck was later abandoned at Sandalpur, and the driver escaped.





INDORE: Khategaon police inspector Dilip Puri was killed in the early hours of Monday when a truck carrying smuggled liquor ran him over during a night-time check on the Indore-Betul highway in Dewas district.Puri, 45, was leading one of five special teams formed by newly posted Dewas SP Aditya Mishra to crack down on the illegal liquor trade.On a tip-off, his team reached the highway around 1.30 am and found a truck parked near Sandalpur Fata, close to the Narmada Dhaba. Puri stepped out of his vehicle and approached the driver. The driver allegedly steered the truck onto the divider to flee, and a rear wheel crushed the inspector.A constable, Sohan Jat, was also injured when the driver allegedly tried to run him over as well. Puri was rushed to hospital but died during treatment. The truck was later abandoned at Sandalpur, and the driver escaped.The vehicle looked empty from outside, but police and Excise officials found a concealed compartment beneath the carrier floor holding 208 boxes, about 1,800 litres of Bagpiper whisky, SP Aditya Mishra said.Chief Minister Mohan Yadav announced Rs 1 crore in assistance for Puri’s family and a compassionate appointment for his wife as a Sub-Inspector. Puri is survived by his wife, a son and a daughter. The state govt has ordered a high-level probe led by Special DG Upendra Jain.The officers followed clues and the trail led quickly to Timarni in Harda district. The seized liquor matched stock at a Sodhalpur Road liquor shop, where officials found 100 boxes of Bagpiper Deluxe whisky bearing the same batch number.Harda Collector Kumar Satyam suspended the shop’s licence, citing a prima facie violation of Section 34(1)(a) of the Madhya Pradesh Excise Act, 1915. Police say the shop was one of three used to run a network supplying illegal liquor to different areas, with this consignment headed to Gujarat.Rahul Jaiswal, described as the network’s kingpin, was taken into custody by late evening. Investigators say he managed the Timarni operation and that all cash from the business was deposited with him, after which he distributed shares to the other partners.In a video statement before his arrest, Rahul denied holding any licence or contract, saying the licence was in the name of Patendra Jaiswal of Barwani and that his own businesses were buses and petrol pumps.Police claim the ownership of the shop is split among Rahul, Manish Jaiswal of Indore and Mohin Jaiswal of Ahmedabad, who hold 30% each, and Patendra Jaiswal, who holds 10%. Police have also detained Vijay Rao of Indore, who allegedly admitted working for Rahul in the smuggling network.In Alirajpur, Kairam Singh was arrested from Behedwa village; he was allegedly travelling in a Swift car ahead of the truck. The truck is registered to Shoaib Qureshi of Khargone, who says he sold it to Suku Ajnaar of Jobat without transferring the registration. Qureshi has been detained.The driver, Gajendra alias Akku Rawat of Alirajpur, remains absconding, with a Rs 10,000 reward announced for information on him.The Excise Commissioner has suspended Timarni Assistant District Excise Officer Amarsingh Baghel and constables Arun Kumre and Krishnapal Singh Dodiyar.Two Timarni shops and one in Rahatgaon remain shut while stocks are checked. “We have identified the source of the liquor, its destination and those involved in transporting it,” said DG Upendra Jain, adding that SPs in five districts have formed teams for raids and arrests.The case comes weeks after more than a dozen suspected hooch deaths in Chandana and Binjana villages in Dewas, which led to action against the district’s SP, collector and Excise officials.
Article Summary: Kategaon police inspector Dilip Puri was killed in the early hours of Monday when a truck carrying smuggled liquor ran him over during a night-time check. Puri, 45, was leading one of five special teams formed by newly posted Dewas SP Aditya Mishra to crack down on the illegal liquor trade. Chief Minister Mohan Yadav announced Rs 1 crore in assistance for Puri’s family.

Article Title: ‘Wife, in-laws responsible’: Meerut man records 8-minute video before dying by suicide; father suffers heart attack on hearing news
Article Text:
The deceased, Prabal Kumar Gupta, was a resident of Patelpuri in the Kankerkhera police station area





MEERUT: A 30-year-old man died during treatment on Sunday night after allegedly consuming a poisonous substance following a dispute with his wife and in-laws. An eight-minute video recorded by him before his death has also surfaced, in which he named his wife and several members of her family, holding them responsible for his condition.The deceased, Prabal Kumar Gupta, was a resident of Patelpuri in the Kankerkhera police station area. His father, Rajiv Gupta, a BJP functionary and resident of the same locality, suffered a heart attack after learning about his son's death. He was rushed to a private hospital, where he is undergoing treatment.Circle officer Daurala Shiv Thakur said, "The man died by suicide following a dispute with his wife and in-laws. The matter was already under mediation through the police, and counselling had been conducted to resolve the differences between the couple."Prabal married Sneha Gupta, a resident of Rishinagar on Rohta Road in the TPNagar police station area, on November 2, 2025. According to family members, differences had developed between the couple soon after their marriage. The two also attended a counselling session at the women's police station on Saturday in an attempt to resolve their marital dispute.According to his family, Prabal left home on his scooter around 11am on Sunday. He allegedly consumed a poisonous substance during the day and recorded a video before being found unconscious in the Sadar police station area. Local residents rushed him to Kailashi Hospital in Kankerkhera. After providing initial treatment, doctors referred him to Subharti Hospital due to his critical condition. He died during treatment there on Sunday night.In the video that surfaced after his death, Prabal spoke about the circumstances leading to his decision and named his wife, Sneha Gupta, her father, brother, aunt and other relatives, holding them responsible for his condition. He also referred to the counselling session held at the women's police station.Shiv Thakur said, "No formal complaint has been received in the matter so far. We are awaiting the postmortem report, while the allegations levelled against police personnel in the video are also being verified. A detailed probe is underway, and further action will be taken based on its findings."
Article Summary: The deceased, Prabal Kumar Gupta, was a resident of Patelpuri in the Kankerkhera police station area. His father, Rajiv Gupta, suffered a heart attack after learning about his son's death. According to family members, differences had developed between the couple soon after their marriage.

Article Title: Thief enters locked First AC coupe, steals Rs 8 lakh jewellery; couple claims no police response despite 3 alarm chain pulls at Lucknow station
Article Text:
Distressed Sunita Kumari shared a video from coupe E of the H1 coach, expressing anger and disappointment over the theft and lack of police response





LUCKNOW: A couple travelling with their one-year-old child in a First AC coach of a train alleged that gold jewellery worth Rs 7-8 lakh and around Rs 35,000 in cash were stolen from their locked coupe at Lucknow's Charbagh railway station in the early hours of November 2.Despite repeated calls to the railway helpline and pulling the alarm chain three times, no GRP or RPF personnel turned up to assist them at the station, the couple claimed.The incident occurred around 1.20am aboard train number 15726, when Umesh Kumar, 31, his wife Sunita Kumari, 30, and their child were travelling from Anand Vihar to Deoria on berths E13 and E14 of H1 coach.Umesh, who works with a private firm in Delhi, married Sunita in 2023. The family, originally from Bhore in Bihar's Gopalganj district, was heading home to celebrate Diwali and Chhath.Speaking to TOI, Umesh said he had fallen asleep on the upper berth while his wife and child were sleeping below. The coupe was locked from inside."My wife suddenly woke up and saw a tall, heavily built man dressed in black standing inside the coupe. He appeared to be putting something into his pocket. When she noticed him, he apologised, claiming he had mistakenly entered the wrong cabin, and walked away," Umesh said.Within a minute, Sunita discovered that her purse had been ransacked and the jewellery and cash were missing."The jewellery was purchased during our wedding. Its present value would be Rs 7-8 lakh. Around Rs 30,000-35,000 in cash was also stolen," Sunita told TOI.Umesh claimed that the intruder had managed to open the coupe door from outside despite its being locked internally.He said police personnel who subsequently met them at Gonda station demonstrated how the door could be opened from outside even when locked from within.Following the theft, Sunita alerted the onboard travelling ticket examiner (TTE), while the couple pulled the alarm chain repeatedly to stop the train from leaving Lucknow."Despite pulling the chain three times and making several calls, no policeman came to help us at Charbagh. We first encountered police personnel at Gonda after contacting emergency helpline 112," Umesh alleged.According to the National Train Enquiry System (NTES), the train, running one hour and 40 minutes late, arrived at platform number two of Charbagh station at 1.15 am and departed for Gonda at 1.35am. The GRP and RPF police stations are located on platform number one.Trains ordinarily have RPF or GRP personnel deployed for security duties. However, it could not immediately be ascertained whether a security squad was present aboard this particular train.Umesh claimed he contacted railway helpline 139 around three times, but the operators only registered his complaint and provided a reference number. No immediate assistance followed, he alleged."By the time they forwarded the complaint, the train would have left the station. I kept asking them how that would help us," he said.The couple subsequently lodged a Zero FIR with GRP Deoria around 9am on November 2.GRP Charbagh SHO Dharamveer Singh told TOI, "We have reached out to the victim to ascertain the sequence of events. The probe is on. The Zero FIR copy is yet to be received from GRP Deoria."TOI also attempted to contact the onboard TTE, from whom the couple had sought assistance, but his phone was switched off.Umesh further claimed that he had noticed frequent movement through the connecting doorway between the First AC coach, the 19th coach from the locomotive, and an adjoining general coach during the journey. He said the doorway was repeatedly opened and closed.Meanwhile, a video of Sunita narrating the incident has surfaced on social media. In the video, she expressed anguish over the lack of police assistance despite repeated calls and alarm chain pulling."This is Yogi's govt, yet there has been no response. Tell me, what am I supposed to do? Nobody is coming to help us. If we are not safe even inside a locked cabin, where will we be safe? Fortunately, my child was not abducted. What would I have done if someone had taken my child?" Sunita said in the video.
Article Summary: Gold jewellery worth Rs 7-8 lakh and around Rs 35,000 in cash were stolen from their locked coupe at Lucknow's Charbagh railway station. Despite repeated calls to the railway helpline and pulling the alarm chain three times, no GRP or RPF personnel turned up to assist them at the station, the couple claimed.

Article Title: Mumbai police impound BMW, seek digital media COO’s licence cancellation for ‘bid to run over’ traffic cop
Article Text:
Juhu's Juhi Mehta found herself in hot water after a parking mishap led to a collision with traffic constable





MUMBAI: Juhu police have impounded the high-end car and asked the regional transport office to cancel the driving licence of Juhu resident Juhi Mehta, who had allegedly hit vehicles and threatened a traffic constable in Vile Parle (West) last week.Mehta, chief operating officer of an online media company, was booked for threatening and obstructing traffic constable Prashant Hake (36) and driving towards him after an accident at Sangeet Mahabharati Junction on Oct 30. She was arrested the next day and later granted bail.Police said fault in the accident remained unclear. Mehta claimed she was trying to park the car to the side to prevent congestion and was uncomfortable stepping out because several people were recording the incident.Hake, attached to Santacruz Traffic Division, said he was regulating traffic near Pratiksha Bungalow in Vile Parle West on Oct 30. Between 8.15pm and 8.30pm, he noticed a crowd gathering at Sangeet Mahabharati Junction. He went to the location and found that a high-end car (driven by Mehta) and a hatchback had had a collision and were blocking traffic.He directed both drivers to move their vehicles aside to clear the obstruction.Hake alleged that Mehta argued with him, verbally abused and threatened him, and tried to leave. When he stood in front of her high-end car and repeatedly asked her to stop, she allegedly accelerated towards him. Hake moved aside and escaped without injury.Mehta allegedly drove away at high speed towards JVPD Junction. A person at the scene recorded the incident, according to the complaint. The hatchback driver, Navinkumar Udaychand Jha (42), told Hake that the high-end car had hit his vehicle from behind. Hake observed damage to its boot, bumper, right taillight, sensor lock and paintwork.Joint commissioner of police, traffic division, Satyanarayan Chaudhary said necessary action was being taken under standard operating procedures.Deputy commissioner of police (Zone West-2) Mohit Garg said further procedures were under way.
Article Summary: Juhi Mehta, chief operating officer of an online media company, was booked for threatening and obstructing traffic constable Prashant Hake. She was arrested the next day and later granted bail. Police impounded her high-end car and asked the regional transport office to cancel her licence.

Article Title: 7,000 offences in eight months: Pune records sharpest jump in drunk driving cases, police promise more patrols
Article Text:
The increase is even more alarming if one were to compare the data with 2023 figures, when only 562 cases were registered

Pune:

TOI

TOI





A policewoman suspended earlier this week for allegedly driving under the influence. A viral video that shows a drunk motorist ramming into multiple two-wheelers. Pune’s problem of drunk driving is once again back in focus, with data now showing that as many as 7,379 offences were registered within just the first eight months of this year, 12% more than last year’s entire total (6,602 cases).The increase is even more alarming if one were to compare the data with 2023 figures, when only 562 cases were registered.Police officialsspoke to said the Jan-Aug numbers are indeed worrisome. “This year’s figures exceed those of all previous years,” said additional commissioner of police, Manoj Patil. “We have been working to control drunk driving, but our efforts have to be intensified, with greater emphasis on night patrols and random checks. This is a serious offence. Lives are at risk,” he said.Residents said drunk motorists were now a common sight in the city. “Almost every evening, we see obvious signs of a vehicle being driven by someone under the influence,” said Vishal Khatir, a working professional who lives in VimannagarHe said that last month he was almost assaulted by a group travelling in a car after he confronted them. “Bystanders came to my rescue.This group stopped the car, surrounded me and threatened to beat me up. Even their speech was slurring. And I have hardly ever seen police patrols in the area,” he said.Animesh Sherkha, a Koregaon Park resident, said drunk driving was commonplace in the area, despite police presence. “It’s indeed a problem, given the number of bars and restaurants here. It’s unfortunate that even after the Porsche incident (in 2024), city police have been unable to clamp down.”A retired RTO officialspoke to said a critical countermeasure could be cancellation of driving licences. “Just last month, the police actually recommended suspension or cancellation of around 1,700 driving licences for serious traffic violations, including drunk driving. In my view, the state government should consider allowing authorities to permanently cancel the licences of anyone caught driving under the influence, without the possibility of reissuance,” the retired official said, adding that such measures could be backed by tougher penalties, including vehicle confiscation, higher fines and imprisonment.Harshad Abhyankar, a member of the Save Pune Traffic Movement said it was time enforcement moved beyond routine checks and fines. “Drink driving is often treated as an issue of indiscipline, prompting the usual suggestions of increased surveillance and higher fines. A dedicated campaign over several months can help curb the problem, but authorities also need to think differently and explore innovative measures,” he said.Salunke Vihar Road resident Atul Pirodkar highlighted another concern: open drinking near liquor shops. “A good example is the shop near my house. I see people drinking in the open every day. Surely, the police are aware of the problem. Residents of NIBM Road Annexe, barely 3 km away, have also been complaining about late-evening disturbances caused by people under the influence of alcohol,” he said.
Article Summary: As many as 7,379 offences were registered within just the first eight months of this year. This is 12% more than last year’s entire total (6,602 cases) The increase is even more alarming if one were to compare the data with 2023 figures, when only 562 cases were registered.
